5: Claims marked *(secondary)* come from a forum or Q&A thread, not from vendor documentation. Claims marked *(measured)* come from the throwaway probes described in §2.1, which are not committed.
6: 
7: ## 1. Recommendation
8: 
9: **Use thin custom Effect adapters for Slack and Microsoft Teams behind the domain `ChannelSender` port. Do not adopt the `Chat` runtime, its `StateAdapter`, or the full `@chat-adapter/*` packages.**
10: 
11: The `Chat` runtime is built for conversational bots (threads, subscriptions, locks, message dedupe), and R3's Channel work is outbound-first plus one slash command. The full adapters do run in workerd (*measured*), but the Teams adapter alone adds about 897 KiB gzip and spent 1.8 s of active startup CPU in the one local profile that finished, against a 1 s Worker startup limit; the `Chat` runtime also needs a `StateAdapter` that SurveyBeat has no Cloudflare-native, tenant-isolated implementation of.
12: 
13: What to build, in order:
14: 
15: 1. **Slack first**, as #295 sequences it. About five endpoints are needed: signature verification (Web Crypto HMAC), `oauth.v2.access`, `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`/`chat.delete`, and `users.lookupByEmail`. All are plain `fetch` calls validated with Effect Schema at the boundary.
16: 2. **Teams second, behind a tenancy spike** (§3.6). The Azure Bot tenancy rules changed in 2025 and a single-tenant bot may not reach other customers' tenants. This is the largest unresolved risk in R3.
17: 3. **No external store, no `StateAdapter`.** Everything an outbound-first Channel needs (installation token, Person-to-Channel binding, sent-message id for later edits) is Organization state and belongs in the Organization Durable Object beside the existing `SendStore`. Redis would break SPEC §6; the Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` that exists today ships in Cloudflare's `agents` package, not in `vercel/chat` (§3.3), and is not worth taking on for a surface this narrow.
18: 4. **Treat `@chat-adapter/{slack,teams}` as reference and test vectors**, not as a dependency. Their stateless subpath modules (`/webhook`, `/api`, `/blocks`, `/cards`) are small, MIT, `fetch`-based and run in workerd with 13.1 KiB gzip (*measured*). Our code is smaller than the cost of tracking a package that shipped seven minor releases between 2026-08-14 and 2026-11-13. If the Channel ADR prefers to reuse them, it must name the package, as AGENTS.md requires, and pin an exact version.
19: 
20: **Revisit this if** a later release wants in-chat conversation (threads, "reply to answer", streaming). Then `chat` plus Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk` state adapter is the route to evaluate, and #295's exclusion of in-chat Answer submission would need its own ADR.
21: 
22: ## 2. Answers to the issue's questions
23: 
24: | Question | Answer | Basis |
25: | --- | --- | --- |
26: | Does `vercel/chat` run on Workers with Alchemy and Effect 4.1.x (`nodejs_compat`)? | Yes, mechanically. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` bundles Slack, Teams and both together, and local workerd serves and rejects bad signatures. It is promise-based, so every call is wrapped in `Effect.tryPromise`. No Alchemy-specific obstacle was found, but I did not deploy through Alchemy. | §2.1, *measured* |
27: | Workerd compatibility and footprint? | Slack full: 277 KiB gz. Teams full: 897 KiB gz, 1.8 s active startup in the one local profile that finished (two others timed out at 10 s). Both: 996 KiB gz. Stateless subpaths: 13 KiB gz. Worker size limit is 64 MiB, so **startup time, not size, is the limiter.** | §2.1, *measured* |
28: | Signature verification and stateless handling in `MainWorker`? | Slack: HMAC-SHA256 with Web Crypto, 5-minute skew, no state. Teams: Microsoft's JWT check, which the stateless subpath does **not** implement; we write it. | §3.2 |
29: | Does it need Redis or another external store? | The `Chat` constructor requires a `StateAdapter`; official ones are Redis, ioredis, Postgres, memory. Redis and Postgres are third-party stores and break SPEC §6. A DO SQLite `StateAdapter` exists but is Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk`, not part of `vercel/chat`. With thin adapters, **no `StateAdapter` is required.** | §3.3 |
30: | Card fidelity? | Slack Block Kit and Teams Adaptive Cards both carry what R3 needs: rating links, a Reminder, a Result summary, and later edits. Plain-link Invitations are possible on both. | §3.4 |
31: | Slack app and Teams bot registration and per-Organization OAuth install? | Slack: standard distributed app plus OAuth v2 install per workspace. Teams: Entra app plus Azure Bot plus Teams app package; per-tenant admin install; tenancy model unresolved. | §3.5, §3.6 |
32: | Teams proactive messages, and where does the conversation reference live? | Needs the bot installed in the Person's personal scope, plus tenant id, user id and service URL. Store the per-Person reference in the **Organization Durable Object**; D1 holds only the tenant-to-Organization routing row. | §3.6 |
33: | Safe Links and the fragment `#t=…&v=…`? | **Not tested.** Microsoft documents that Teams links are checked at click time and not rewritten, and says nothing about fragments. Treat as unverified and gating for Teams. | §3.7 |
34: | Slack plain links and `block_actions`? | Slack documents `block_actions` as the payload for Block Kit interactive components, and a URL button still sends one. Plain `<url\|text>` links in message text are not interactive components. **Slack does not state "plain links send nothing" in so many words;** the conclusion follows from its payload list and is a one-click live check. | §3.8 |
35: 
36: ### 2.1 How the footprint was measured
37: 
38: In a scratch directory outside the repository I installed the four 4.45.0 packages (plus `@chat-adapter/state-memory`) and wrote five tiny Worker entries. Each used `compatibility_date = 2026-11-01` and `nodejs_compat`, wrangler 4.165.0, Node 26.
39: 
40: | Entry | `wrangler deploy --dry-run` | Local `wrangler check startup`, active CPU |
41: | --- | --- | --- |
42: | Stateless subpaths only (`slack/webhook`, `slack/api`, `slack/blocks`, `teams/api`, `teams/cards`, `teams/webhook`) | 56.5 KiB / **13.1 KiB gz** | 19 / 99 / 59 ms |
43: | `Chat` + Slack adapter + memory state | 1,324 KiB / **277 KiB gz** | 232 / 93 / 63 ms |
44: | `Chat` + Teams adapter + memory state | 4,839 KiB / **897 KiB gz** | 1,795 ms; the other two runs timed out at 10 s |
45: | `Chat` + Slack + Teams + memory state | 5,332 KiB / **996 KiB gz** | 952 / 449 / 700 ms |
46: | For scale: Effect HttpApi Worker (`docs/research/effect-on-workers.md`) | about 86 KiB gz | 54–61 ms |
47: 
48: Caveats that matter:
49: 
50: - Startup numbers are **local workerd on a shared, noisy machine**, so they are indicative only. Cloudflare warns that production CPUs differ, and `docs/research/effect-on-workers.md` makes the same point. The Worker startup limit is 1 s ([Workers limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/)). A Teams adapter that sometimes needs more than a second locally is not a safe thing to load into `MainWorker`.
51: - The Worker size limit on both plans is 64 MiB (same page), so 1 MiB gzip is not a size problem. It is a startup-parse and review-surface problem.
52: - Behaviour check in local workerd: `bot.webhooks.slack` returned `401 Invalid signature` for a bad signature, and `bot.webhooks.teams` returned `401` for a missing `Authorization` header. That proves the modules load and the rejection path works. **It does not prove a valid inbound activity or an outbound send**, which need real Slack and Azure credentials.
53: - Why the Teams adapter is so heavy: its dependencies are `@microsoft/teams.apps` (needs Node ≥ 22.12; depends on `express`, `axios`, `jsonwebtoken`, `jwks-rsa`, `@azure/msal-node`, `@microsoft/signalr`, `reflect-metadata`) plus `teams.api`, `teams.cards`, `teams.graph` and `teams.graph-endpoints` ([npm metadata](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/teams.apps)). Slack's full adapter pulls `@slack/web-api` and `@slack/socket-mode`.
54: 
55: ## 3. Evidence
56: 
57: ### 3.1 What `vercel/chat` is
58: 
59: - Chat SDK is a TypeScript bot framework: a `Chat` instance holds platform adapters and one state adapter; handlers such as `bot.onNewMention` and `onSubscribedMessage` run for events from every adapter, and each adapter exposes `bot.webhooks.<name>` ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)). Repository: [vercel/chat](https://github.com/vercel/chat), MIT.
60: - The state adapter "share[s] subscriptions, locks, and cached data across requests" (same page). Core `Chat` calls it on every inbound message: `setIfNotExists` for `dedupe:<adapter>:<messageId>` and `acquireLock` per thread (read in `chat@4.45.0` `dist/index.js`).
61: - Release cadence is fast: 4.38.0 on 2026-08-14 to 4.45.0 on 2026-11-13. The docs warn that protected members of official adapters "can change in minor releases, so pin the adapter version" ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)).
62: - The repo already pins Effect and Alchemy together because both are unstable or beta (ADR 0008). A third fast-moving dependency in the send path is a cost, not a saving, for a surface of about five calls per platform.
63: 
64: ### 3.2 Webhook verification and stateless handling in `MainWorker`
65: 
66: **Slack.** Requests carry `x-slack-request-timestamp` and `x-slack-signature`; the adapter verifies `v0=` + HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:<timestamp>:<body>` with `crypto.subtle`, and rejects a timestamp more than 300 s off (`@chat-adapter/slack@4.45.0`, `dist/chunk-KYABMAGK.js`). This is stateless and about 40 lines in Effect with Web Crypto. Slack must receive an acknowledgement within 3 seconds for interaction payloads ([handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/)); a slash command should ack immediately and post the answer through `response_url`, which accepts up to 5 posts within 30 minutes (same page). `MainWorker` must read the raw body once and verify before parsing.
67: 
68: **Teams.** Microsoft requires the bot to verify a JWT on every inbound request: `Authorization: Bearer`, issuer `https://api.botframework.com`, audience equal to the bot's app id, within validity (5-minute skew), RS256 signature from the keys at `https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/keys`, and a `serviceUrl` claim equal to the activity's `serviceUrl`. The page calls requirements 4 and 6 (signature and serviceUrl) "particularly" important ([Bot Connector authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication)). The stateless `@chat-adapter/teams/webhook` subpath **only parses** activities; it contains no JWT, JWKS or OpenID code (grep of the 4.45.0 `dist`). JWT verification lives in the heavy `@microsoft/teams.apps` path. So the thin route has to write this check either way. It needs `crypto.subtle` RS256 verify, a cached JWKS fetch, and the `serviceUrl` claim match. The single-tenant variant (tenant-specific issuer and metadata) was not confirmed from documentation; see §5.
69: 
70: **Useful guard to copy from the Teams adapter:** it refuses to send a bot token to any `serviceUrl` outside an allowlist (`smba.trafficmanager.net` and the GCC, DoD and China hosts) or a loopback emulator (`dist/chunk-4NNW2LU4.js`). `serviceUrl` arrives in the inbound activity, so an unchecked value is a token-exfiltration path.
71: 
72: **Where it runs.** Both verifications are request-local and stateless, so they can sit in `MainWorker` beside the Better Auth routes, with each route's classification added to `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`. The Submission Worker stays untouched; no Channel traffic may reach it (ADR 0005).
73: 
74: ### 3.3 State storage
75: 
76: - `Chat` takes `state` in its config and uses it for dedupe and locks (§3.1). The official state adapters are Redis, ioredis, PostgreSQL and memory; the docs tell Vercel deployments to use Redis, ioredis or PostgreSQL, because memory "loses state on restart and two instances can process the same thread at once" ([Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/chat-sdk/adapters)). **Redis and Postgres are third-party stores and break SPEC §6, so `vercel/chat` cannot be used with its official state adapters.**
77: - A Durable Object SQLite adapter does exist, but it is not part of `vercel/chat`. Cloudflare's `agents` package exports `createChatSdkState()` and a `ChatSdkStateAgent` sub-agent that store subscriptions, locks, queues, dedupe keys, thread state and history in Durable Object SQLite ([Cloudflare docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/agent-class/communication-channels/chat-sdk/); listed as vendor-official in [vercel/chat#669](https://github.com/vercel/chat/issues/669)). Costs for SurveyBeat:
78:   - it requires the `agents` package (version 0.33.0 today; peer dependencies include `ai`, `zod`, `chat`, `react` and `vite`), a parent `Agent` Durable Object class, and the `ChatSdkStateAgent` class exported from the Worker entry. SurveyBeat's classes come from Alchemy's generated entry (AGENTS.md notes the same constraint for #247), so this is untested friction;
79:   - state shards are keyed by platform thread or channel id (`slack:C123`), not by Organization, so chat state would live **outside** the per-Organization Durable Object that SPEC §6.2 makes the system of record;
80:   - `vercel/chat` itself does not consider the adapter part of its CLI scaffold (`CLI_INCOMPATIBLE_ADAPTERS` in #669), so it is a supported-but-unusual combination.
84: ### 3.4 Card fidelity
101: ### 3.5 Slack app and per-Organization install
111: ### 3.6 Teams registration, proactive messages, and the tenancy risk
134: ### 3.7 Teams Safe Links and the URL fragment
154: ### 3.8 Slack: plain links and `block_actions`

176: ## 5. What I could not verify

The window closed in the seconds between the monitor firing and the command.

Another agent started Organization.test.ts and a gate. The command already exited with code 2. I will restart the monitor and wait again. I cannot commit without the hook. I am considering waiting for specific PIDs to serialize.

The monitor already serializes by PID. The commit failed because another suite grabbed the ports in the gap. The working tree is clean. I will restart the watcher and commit immediately in the same shell when the next wake arrives.

I considered embedding the commit directly inside the monitor script to eliminate the gap between detection and execution. That would cause gate output to wake the monitor on every line, so it is not viable.

I can redirect the commit script's stdout and stderr to a log file. The monitor will then stay quiet until the final line, eliminating the wake-on-every-line problem. This allows the commit to run directly inside the monitor script.

The commit and push will run inside the monitor script itself. The check and commit execute in the same shell, so the race window shrinks to milliseconds. If another process grabs the ports in that instant, the hook fails and the monitor reports FAILED. I can then retry.

I am writing the updated monitor script now. It will run the commit and push directly inside the loop, redirecting all hook output to a log file so the monitor stays silent. I will add `set -e` inside the commit block so a failed commit does not push. The script will also suppress periodic status prints to stdout.

The monitor script now rechecks busy processes and open ports immediately before running the commit. If either has changed, it skips the commit and waits. This closes the race window between the initial check and the actual git command.

The script now checks for stray untracked files before committing. It adds only the research note, commits with the message from /tmp/pr-317-commit.txt, and pushes to origin HEAD. The final SHA is captured and logged.

The monitor script now handles three outcomes: a successful commit, a lost window that triggers a 15-second retry, and a failed commit that exits with an error. It also logs periodic busy and port states to the log file. I confirmed the commit message file was written before the busy check, so it remains available for the next attempt.

The commit message file was never written because the previous run exited at the busy check. I need to create it now. The monitor script does not use `set -e`, so the lost-window exit code is captured and the loop continues.

I realized `{ }` is not a subshell, so `exit 20` would kill the entire monitor script. I will wrap the commit block in parentheses instead. If the commit hook fails because of a test failure rather than a port collision, the script will report FAILED and stop so I can inspect the log. Only a port collision will trigger an automatic retry.

I will retry only when the log shows a port collision or SQLITE_BUSY. Real test failures will stop the monitor so I can inspect the output. I will check only the latest attempt section to avoid false positives from older logs.
Another suite took ports 1337 and 1338 before the commit started. The next attempt will commit from the watcher itself, so there is no gap.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
DIR=~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks
LOG=$DIR/commit_317.log
WT=/home/ubuntu/.t3/worktrees/surveybeat-next/t3-c7cc7cf2-3e10cd6c806d0ae2
attempts=0
while :; do
  busy=$(ps -eo cmd | grep -E "scripts/fence/gate.mjs|vitest run --project unit" | grep -v grep | wc -l)
  ports=$(ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E ':1337|:1338' | wc -l)
  if [ "$busy" -eq 0 ] && [ "$ports" -eq 0 ]; then
    attempts=$((attempts + 1))
    (
      set -euo pipefail
      echo "=== attempt $attempts $(date -Is) ==="
      cd "$WT"
      busy2=$(ps -eo cmd | grep -E "scripts/fence/gate.mjs|vitest run --project unit" | grep -v grep | wc -l)
      ports2=$(ss -ltn 2>/dev/null | grep -E ':1337|:1338' | wc -l)
      echo "recheck busy=$busy2 ports=$ports2"
      if [ "$busy2" -ne 0 ] || [ "$ports2" -ne 0 ]; then
        exit 20
      fi
      others=$(git status --short | grep -v 'docs/research/r3-mcp-auth.md' || true)
      if [ -n "$others" ]; then
        echo "unexpected files: $others"
        exit 3
      fi
      git add -- docs/research/r3-mcp-auth.md
      git commit -F /tmp/pr-317-commit.txt
      git push -u origin HEAD || git push -v -u origin HEAD
      git rev-parse HEAD
      git status --short
      git log -1 --oneline
    ) >> "$LOG" 2>&1
    code=$?
    if [ "$code" -eq 0 ]; then
      sha=$(git -C "$WT" rev-parse --short HEAD)
      echo "ACTION_REQUIRED: COMMIT_OK $sha log=$LOG"
      exit 0
    fi
    if [ "$code" -eq 20 ]; then
      printf '%s lost window on attempt %s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$attempts" >> "$LOG"
    elif tail -n 80 "$LOG" | grep -E "already in use|EADDRINUSE|SQLITE_BUSY" >/dev/null; then
      printf '%s port collision on attempt %s (exit %s)\n' "$(date -Is)" "$attempts" "$code" >> "$LOG"
    else
      echo "FAILED: commit exited $code on attempt $attempts, see $LOG"
      exit 1
    fi
    if [ "$attempts" -ge 8 ]; then
      echo "FAILED: gave up after $attempts attempts, see $LOG"
      exit 1
    fi
    sleep 20
    continue
  fi
  printf '%s busy=%s port_lines=%s\n' "$(date -Is)" "$busy" "$ports" >> "$LOG"
  sleep 30
done

**Verdict: APPROVE.** I found no factual error that would change the recommendation. The minor fixes below would make it more accurate, and none of them blocks a merge.

The PR changes one file, `docs/research/r3-vercel-chat-adapters.md` (+194). It doesn't touch SPEC, the ADRs, product code or dependencies.

## What I confirmed

- **Issue #297 coverage:** the note answers all five original questions and all four 2026-11-20 additions, in the §2 table and §3.3, §3.6, §3.7 and §3.8.
- **Package claims, checked against the 4.45.0 tarballs and npm metadata:**
  - 4.45.0 was published 2026-11-13 and 4.38.0 on 2026-08-14.
  - Slack signature check: `v0:${timestamp}:${body}` with `crypto.subtle` HMAC and `maxSkewSeconds ?? 300`, in `chunk-KYABMAGK.js`.
  - The Teams package's `dist` contains no JWT, JWKS or OpenID code, so a thin adapter has to write that check.
  - `TRUSTED_CONNECTOR_HOSTS` is in `chunk-4NNW2LU4.js`.
  - The README says `appType` defaults to `"MultiTenant"` and lists "Slash commands | No" for Teams.
  - `link-button` renders a `button` with `url` and an `action_id`. `link` renders a `section` with `<url|label>`.
  - Core `Chat` writes the `dedupe:${adapter.name}:${message.id}` key and calls `acquireLock`.
  - The `@microsoft/teams.apps` 2.2.1 dependencies and `node >=22.12.0` match the note. `agents` 0.33.0 has peer dependencies on `ai`, `zod`, `chat`, `react` and `vite`.
- **Vendor docs:**
  - Workers startup limit is 1 s and the size limit is 64 MiB on both plans.
  - Slack button docs: "If you're using url, you'll still receive an interaction payload…".
  - Slack interactions: 3 s acknowledgement, and `response_url` takes up to 5 posts within 30 minutes.
  - Bot registration: "Multi-tenant bot creation will be deprecated after July 31, 2025."
  - Safe Links in Teams: "URLs aren't rewritten", and the intermediary-page sentence exists.
  - Proactive messages: 403 `ForbiddenOperationException`, and "store the tenantId and then store either the userId, or channelId".
  - `validDomains` and the "URL may lead to untrusted content" warning.
  - Vercel's state adapter list and memory-adapter warning.
  - Cloudflare's `createChatSdkState` and `ChatSdkStateAgent`.
  - Slack rate limits, `expires_in: 43200` and lookup Tier 3.
- **SPEC §6 and ADR 0005 hold:**
  - Redis and Postgres are rejected.
  - The conversation reference goes in the Organization Durable Object, and D1 gets only the routing row that SPEC §6.2 names.
  - The Submission Worker is untouched.
  - The token stays in the fragment.
  - The no-token-plus-Edit-key rule is restated correctly.
- **Glossary:** "user" appears only as a platform user id, and "survey content" copies SPEC §6.2's wording. There is no Survey, Response or instance drift. The note never mentions MCP, so it does not stray into #302.
- **Safe Links:** the section is labeled untested, says both `#t=` and `&v=` would be lost together, and treats that as blocking for Teams rather than a degraded mode.
- **Tenancy:** both Q&A threads are labeled *(secondary)*, and the ADR is not committed to a tenancy model.
- **Measured figures:** they are labeled local, noisy and from one profile, and §5 says to re-measure on a preview stage.
- **What wasn't tested:** §5 says plainly that Alchemy wasn't used, and that no valid inbound event or outbound send was tested.

## Factual errors that change the recommendation

None.

## Minor inaccuracies

1. **Bot Framework requirement numbers are wrong.** The note says: "The page calls requirements 4 and 6 (signature and serviceUrl) 'particularly' important." Microsoft's list has seven items: Bearer header, JWT, issuer, audience, validity, signature, serviceUrl. The page says "All of these requirements are important, particularly requirements 4 and 6", so 4 and 6 are **audience and signature**. The serviceUrl claim is item 7. Constraint 7 still lists every check, so the design isn't affected, but this sentence is security-relevant.
2. **Two Slack sentences state the plain-link result as fact,** although §3.8 is careful elsewhere:
   - §3.4: "A plain link produces no event."
   - §3.8: "its plain `link` element renders as a `section` with `<url|label>` and does not."

   Both should say this is inferred from Slack's payload list until the live check runs, as the §2 table and the last bullet of §3.8 already do.
3. **Q&A 5882874 is undersold.** The note cites it only for "strongly recommended" AppSource publishing. The same answer says: "When the bot attempts to send a proactive message to a conversation in Tenant B, that token is not valid for the target tenant, and the Bot Framework therefore rejects the request." That is the most direct evidence on the open question, though still secondary, and it makes the tenancy risk stronger.
4. **Q&A 5896006 attribution is off.** The note says the answers come from "a Microsoft external-staff moderator and an MVP" and point to the workarounds. On the page, the workaround lists come from two moderators. The MVP answer offers no workaround and says only Microsoft can grant an exception. The "Microsoft 365 Agent / Copilot extensibility" mention is there, but I couldn't confirm who wrote it.
5. **The `extractTeamsContinuation` shape is incomplete.** The note gives `{ conversationId, serviceUrl, tenantId, teamId?, channelId? }`. The code also returns optional `activityId` and `replyToId`, and `tenantId` is optional too.
6. **One allowlist host is missing.** The note says "`smba.trafficmanager.net` and the GCC, DoD and China hosts". The set also includes the government host `smba.infra.gov.teams.microsoft.us`.
7. **The table name is wrong.** The note says "the Person rows (`people`, email)", but the Durable Object table is `person` (`0003_person.sql`).
8. **One glossary drift.** "tenant-isolated implementation" (§1) uses Tenant for Organization, which the glossary avoids. "Organization-isolated" fits better. Tenant in the Microsoft sense is fine everywhere else.
9. **One AGENTS.md citation stretches the rule.** The note says the Channel ADR "must name the package, as AGENTS.md requires". AGENTS.md says that only about adding a Ratstack *template* package. The point is still sound under ADR 0008's pinning, but the citation is a stretch.

## Gaps worth adding

- **SPEC §5.1 and §5.7 conflict with plain links.** §5.1 says "In Slack and Teams, the message has interactive buttons and, where the platform allows it, a modal", and §5.7 says "Members can answer from the messages". #295's review decision and the note's constraint 3 require plain links and no buttons. The note should say the Channel ADR, or a SPEC edit, has to reconcile this, as AGENTS.md asks when a change contradicts the spec. Otherwise the ADR inherits a silent contradiction.
- **The Safe Links test plan can't meet constraint 6.** Constraint 6 gates Teams on proof that the fragment "is not sent to Microsoft". The §3.7 plan only reads `location.hash` on the answer page, which shows whether the fragment survives, not whether Microsoft receives it. The note should either say how the second risk would be shown, or narrow the gate to survival and leave the exposure question to the ADR. As written, the gate may be impossible to pass.

## UNVERIFIED

These are unconfirmed, not shown to be wrong:

- All probe measurements: the bundle sizes, the startup CPU figures and the 401 rejection paths. The probes are not committed.
- Safe Links behavior with the fragment, and whether Adaptive Card links are treated like typed links.
- Whether a single-tenant bot can send proactive messages into other tenants. No Microsoft document settles it either way.
- Whether `Action.OpenUrl` sends any activity to the bot. The cards page describes only "Opens a URL in the user's browser."
- The Adaptive Card action limit, and whether DMs need `im:write`. The `chat.postMessage` page lists only `chat:write` and says passing a user id opens a DM.
- These quoted phrases, which I didn't find in what I scraped: "links in Teams conversations, group chats, or from channels" (the page says "chats, group chats, channels, and tabs") and the Built-in-preset-for-Teams sentence.
- The Slack distribution and Marketplace claims, and the `link_shared` quote.

matches.content: The `Chat` runtime is built for conversational bots (threads, subscriptions, locks, message dedupe), and R3's Channel work is outbound-first plus one slash command. The full adapters do run in workerd (*measured*), but the Teams adapter alone adds about 897 KiB gzip and spent 1.8 s of active startup CPU in the one local profile that finished, against a 1 s Worker startup limit; the `Chat` runtime also needs a `StateAdapter` that SurveyBeat has no Cloudflare-native, tenant-isolated implementation of.

4. **Treat `@chat-adapter/{slack,teams}` as reference and test vectors**, not as a dependency. Their stateless subpath modules (`/webhook`, `/api`, `/blocks`, `/cards`) are small, MIT, `fetch`-based and run in workerd with 13.1 KiB gzip (*measured*). Our code is smaller than the cost of tracking a package that shipped seven minor releases between 2026-08-14 and 2026-11-13. If the Channel ADR prefers to reuse them, it must name the package, as AGENTS.md requires, and pin an exact version.

| Slack plain links and `block_actions`? | Slack documents `block_actions` as the payload for Block Kit interactive components, and a URL button still sends one. Plain `<url\|text>` links in message text are not interactive components. **Slack does not state "plain links send nothing" in so many words;** the conclusion follows from its payload list and is a one-click live check. | §3.8 |

**Teams.** Microsoft requires the bot to verify a JWT on every inbound request: `Authorization: Bearer`, issuer `https://api.botframework.com`, audience equal to the bot's app id, within validity (5-minute skew), RS256 signature from the keys at `https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/keys`, and a `serviceUrl` claim equal to the activity's `serviceUrl`. The page calls requirements 4 and 6 (signature and serviceUrl) "particularly" important ([Bot Connector authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication)). The stateless `@chat-adapter/teams/webhook` subpath **only parses** activities; it contains no JWT, JWKS or OpenID code (grep of the 4.45.0 `dist`). JWT verification lives in the heavy `@microsoft/teams.apps` path. So the thin route has to write this check either way. It needs `crypto.subtle` RS256 verify, a cached JWKS fetch, and the `serviceUrl` claim match. The single-tenant variant (tenant-specific iss [... truncated (1031 chars total)]

**Useful guard to copy from the Teams adapter:** it refuses to send a bot token to any `serviceUrl` outside an allowlist (`smba.trafficmanager.net` and the GCC, DoD and China hosts) or a loopback emulator (`dist/chunk-4NNW2LU4.js`). `serviceUrl` arrives in the inbound activity, so an unchecked value is a token-exfiltration path.

**What the Invitation needs** (from #295): plain links only, link previews off, five rating links that open `answer.html#t=<token>&v=<1–5>`, an "Open check-in" link, a Reminder in the same shape, an edit that removes answer links once the member answers or the Round closes (#298), and a Result summary posted only after the Result is shared, with no comments, counts or Discussion guide.

**Why plain links are a privacy requirement, not just a style choice.** A Slack button click sends `block_actions` to `MainWorker`, with the clicking Slack user id and a timestamp. That is a Person-bound, timed event for "opened the rating link on Round R" at the moment of answering, delivered to the Worker that has logs, while ADR 0005 keeps all of that off the Submission path. A plain link produces no event.

- SurveyBeat must send to Persons in **many customers' tenants** from one bot. A Microsoft Q&A thread *(secondary)* from an ISV with about 100 tenants says the documented single-tenant model "does not provide the cross-tenant outbound capability" their SaaS needs; the answers (a Microsoft external-staff moderator and an MVP) point to a single-tenant bot distributed as a Teams app that other tenants install, user-assigned managed identity, or the newer Microsoft 365 Agents route, without stating that single-tenant outbound to other tenants works ([Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5896006/request-for-exception-to-provision-new-multi-tenan)). Another thread *(secondary)* says publishing through AppSource is "strongly recommended" for external tenants with a single-tenant bot ([Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5882874/clarification-on-multi-tenant-support-for-single-t)).

- The page says to store the `tenantId` and either the `userId` or `channelId`. The adapter's stored shape is `{ conversationId, serviceUrl, tenantId, teamId?, channelId? }` (`extractTeamsContinuation`).

- **Organization Durable Object**, in a `channel_binding` table keyed by Person: `channel`, the platform ids above, and the Slack/Teams message ids of each send. Reasons: it identifies a Person, so it belongs with the Person rows (`people`, email) that already live there; deleting a Person then deletes their bindings in one place; the send path already runs through the Organization object (`SendStore`); and it keeps D1 small.

- A button that has a `url` is still an interactive component: "If you're using url, you'll still receive an interaction payload and will need to send an acknowledgement response" ([button element](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/button-element/)). **So link buttons do send `block_actions` to our Request URL; plain links do not need to be buttons.** The Chat SDK's `link-button` renders as a `button` with `url` and an `action_id` (`@chat-adapter/slack` `blocks.js`), so it would trigger this; its plain `link` element renders as a `section` with `<url|label>` and does not.

- **What is not stated.** Slack does not publish a sentence of the form "clicking a plain link sends nothing to the app". The conclusion rests on the payload list above. Unfurling is a separate matter: with `unfurl_links` left on, Slack's servers may fetch the URL (they send no fragment); set `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` to false as #295 requires. A live check costs a few minutes: post a message with five plain links to a dev workspace, subscribe the Request URL to a request log, click each, and confirm zero requests.

6. **The token stays in the fragment, and Teams is gated on proof.** Link shape is unchanged: `…/a#t=<token>[&v=<1–5>]`. Teams ships only after the Safe Links spike (§3.7) shows the fragment survives and is not sent to Microsoft; otherwise the ADR must pick another handoff. ADR 0007's rule that the link only preselects and the answer saves on confirm applies unchanged.

- **Slack:** the exact scope set for opening a DM (`im:write` versus `chat:write` alone); the Marketplace review policy for listing; behaviour of `users.lookupByEmail` for guests and Slack Connect users; and the live "no event on plain link click" check (§3.8).

- Microsoft: <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/safe-links-about>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/bots/how-to/conversations/send-proactive-messages>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/task-modules-and-cards/cards/cards-actions>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/bot-service-quickstart-registration>, <https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication>. Secondary: Microsoft Q&A threads 5896006 and 5882874.

145→What it does not say: whether the validation request includes the fragment, whether the intermediary redirect keeps it, or whether links inside a bot's Adaptive Card are treated like links in a typed message. A browser inherits the original fragment across an HTTP 3xx redirect when the `Location` header carries none (RFC 9110 §10.2.2), but the page does not say the intermediary uses a 3xx rather than a script redirect.

Two separate risks follow:

1. **The fragment is lost.** `#t=…` and `&v=…` share one fragment, so the likely failure is that both are lost, not just `&v=`. The issue's fallback ("Open check-in only") still needs the token. If the fragment does not survive, the Teams Invitation has no anonymous-safe handoff to `answer.html`. The Channel ADR must treat that as **blocking for Teams**, not as a degraded mode.
150→2. **The fragment reaches Microsoft.** If the click-time check sends the full URL to Microsoft's service, the Invitation token (ADR 0005 keeps it in the fragment so that no scanner or log ever sees it) is exposed to a third party. Email already has the same unknown; this note adds no evidence either way.

Test plan for the spike: in a Defender-licensed test tenant with Teams protection on, post a bot Adaptive Card whose link is `https://<preview-stage>/a#t=TEST&v=3`; click it from desktop, web and mobile; read `location.hash` on the answer page (it can log nothing but its own hash to the console for the test); repeat with the protection setting off as a control; and repeat with the link in a `TextBlock` and in `Action.OpenUrl`. Expected cost: half a day plus a tenant.

### 3.8 Slack: plain links and `block_actions`

- The Slack interaction docs list `block_actions` as the payload for a "Block Kit interactive component", alongside shortcuts, `view_submission` and `view_closed` ([handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/)).
- A button that has a `url` is still an interactive component: "If you're using url, you'll still receive an interaction payload and will need to send an acknowledgement response" ([button element](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/button-element/)). **So link buttons do send `block_actions` to our Request URL; plain links do not need to be buttons.** The Chat SDK's `link-button` renders as a `button` with `url` and an `action_id` (`@chat-adapter/slack` `blocks.js`), so it would trigger this; its plain `link` element renders as a `section` with `<url|label>` and does not.
- The Events API `link_shared` event is sent "when a link — matching the registered URL domain your app is setup to track — is posted", not when it is clicked; it also requires a subscription and a registered domain, and apps do not receive it for their own messages ([link_shared](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/link_shared/)). SurveyBeat should register no unfurl domain and subscribe to no `link_shared`.
- **What is not stated.** Slack does not publish a sentence of the form "clicking a plain link sends nothing to the app". The conclusion rests on the payload list above. Unfurling is a separate matter: with `unfurl_links` left on, Slack's servers may fetch the URL (they send no fragment); set `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` to false as #295 requires. 1. **The fragment is lost.** `#t=…` and `&v=…` share one fragment, so the likely failure is that both are lost, not just `&v=`. The issue's fallback ("Open check-in only") still needs the token. 2. **The fragment reaches Microsoft.** If the click-time check sends the full URL to Microsoft's service, the Invitation token (ADR 0005 keeps it in the fragment so that no scanner or log ever sees it) is exposed to a third party. ### 3.8 Slack: plain links and `block_actions`

- The Slack interaction docs list `block_actions` as the payload for a "Block Kit interactive component", alongside shortcuts, `view_submission` and `view_closed` ([handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/)).
- A button that has a `url` is still an interactive component: "If you're using url, you'll still receive an interaction payload and will need to send an acknowledgement response" ([button element](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/button-element/)). **So link buttons do send `block_actions` to our Request URL; plain links do not need to be buttons.** The Chat SDK's `link-button` renders as a `button` with `url` and an `action_id` (`@chat-adapter/slack` `blocks.js`), so it would trigger this; its plain `link` element renders as a `section` with `<url|label>` and does not.
- The Events API `link_shared` event is sent "when a link — matching the registered URL domain your app is setup to track — is posted", not when it is clicked; it also requires a subscription and a registered domain, and apps do not receive it for their own messages ([link_shared](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/link_shared/)). SurveyBeat should register no unfurl domain and subscribe to no `link_shared`.
- **What is not stated.** Slack does not publish a sentence of the form "clicking a plain link sends nothing to the app". The conclusion rests on the payload list above. Unfurling is a separate matter: with `unfurl_links` left on, Slack's servers may fetch the URL (they send no fragment); set `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` to false as #295 requires. A live check costs a few minutes: post a message with five plain links to a dev workspace, subscribe the Request URL to a request log, click each, and confirm zero requests.

## 4. Constraints the Channel ADR must keep

1. **Port, not product.** `ChannelSender` stays in `packages/domain` with no Slack, Teams or Cloudflare imports; Slack and Teams senders live in `packages/cloudflare` (boundary rules, ADR 0008). The domain port speaks Invitation, Reminder and Result summary, not "message" or "thread".
2. **No third-party store, no `Chat` runtime in `MainWorker`.** If a later ADR adopts `chat`, it must also name the `StateAdapter` and show it is Cloudflare-only (the Cloudflare `agents` adapter, or one we write over the Organization Durable Object).
3. **Plain links only, previews off.** No Block Kit buttons (including `url` buttons) and no Adaptive Card `Action.Submit`/`Action.Execute`. Slack: `unfurl_links:false`, `unfurl_media:false`, no `link_shared` subscription. Teams: `Action.OpenUrl` or markdown links only. This keeps every chat click out of `MainWorker`, so no Channel click event carries a Person and a time (ADR 0005, ADR 0007).
4. **Where state lives.** The per-Person binding (Slack user id; Teams `tenantId`, `userId`, `serviceUrl`, `conversationId`), the workspace token (encrypted with a Worker secret, like `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY`), and the sent-message ids for later edits live in the Organization Durable Object. D1 holds only `slack:<teamId>` and `teams:<tenantId>` → `organizationId`. Deleting a Person deletes their bindings. No survey content, Answer or Result in D1.
5. **Zero-Leakage Handoff stays.** Chat Channels deliver Invitations, Reminders and shared Result summaries only. Answers still confirm on `answer.html` through the Submission Worker. Nothing in the Channel path may carry both an Invitation token and an Edit key, and no Channel route is served by the Submission Worker.
6. **The token stays in the fragment, and Teams is gated on proof.** Link shape is unchanged: `…/a#t=<token>[&v=<1–5>]`. Teams ships only after the Safe Links spike (§3.7) shows the fragment survives and is not sent to Microsoft; otherwise the ADR must pick another handoff. ADR 0007's rule that the link only preselects and the answer saves on confirm applies unchanged.
7. **Verify before parse, on every inbound route.** Slack: HMAC-SHA256, 300 s skew, raw body. Teams: the Bot Framework JWT checks in §3.2, including the `serviceUrl` claim, and an allowlist of Connector hosts before any outbound call. Each route is classified in `PrivacyRegistry.ts`.
8. **Idempotent, queued sends.** Sends go through the existing Queue and `SendStore` pattern: one send id per Person and Round, retry-safe, with per-workspace pacing for Slack's rate limit and a visible failure state when a Person has no binding (not a silent fall back to a different Channel that the Person did not pick).
9. **Member-visible disclosure.** The ADR should require plain wording that sending an Invitation through Slack or Teams is a third-party data flow, and that Slack lookup uses the Person's email (`users:read.email`).
10. **Slack before Teams, Teams behind two spikes:** the tenancy spike (§3.6) and the Safe Links spike (§3.7). Slash command design for Teams (bot command or message extension) is a separate item.
11. **Edits remove links.** Both platforms support editing a sent message by stored id, which #298 relies on; the binding must therefore keep the Slack `channel` + `ts` and the Teams `conversationId` + `activityId` for each send.
12. **One workspace, one Organization.** Reject installing a Slack workspace or Teams tenant that is already bound to another Organization.

## 5. What I could not verify

- **Teams Safe Links and the fragment.** No tenant, no Defender licence. Only the documentation in §3.7 was read.
- **Teams tenancy.** Whether one single-tenant Azure Bot can send proactive messages into other customers' tenants. Microsoft documentation does not answer it; the evidence is two Q&A threads *(secondary)*.
- **Valid-path behaviour of any adapter.** No Slack workspace or Azure Bot was available. I verified bundling, loading and the 401 rejection paths in local workerd, not a verified inbound event or an outbound `postMessage`/`createConversation`.
- **Alchemy deployment.** I used `wrangler` for bundling and local workerd. I did not deploy any of these through Alchemy or run them inside the repository's `MainWorker`.
- **Production startup CPU.** Startup numbers are local, on a shared machine, and varied by up to 4× between runs. Re-measure on a deployed preview stage if the Channel ADR leans on them.
- **Slack:** the exact scope set for opening a DM (`im:write` versus `chat:write` alone); the Marketplace review policy for listing; behaviour of `users.lookupByEmail` for guests and Slack Connect users; and the live "no event on plain link click" check (§3.8).
- **Teams:** the per-card action limit; whether `Action.OpenUrl` triggers any bot activity; the Graph permission names needed to install the app proactively for a Person; and the single-tenant variants of the inbound JWT issuer and metadata.
- **`@chat-adapter/*` as a reference.** I read the 4.45.0 `dist` bundles, not the TypeScript source or tests in the repository.

- Cloudflare Agents `agents/chat-sdk`: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/agents/agent-class/communication-channels/chat-sdk/>. Workers limits: <https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/>.

**What the Invitation needs** (from #295): plain links only, link previews off, five rating links that open `answer.html#t=<token>&v=<1–5>`, an "Open check-in" link, a Reminder in the same shape, an edit that removes answer links once the member answers or the Round closes (#298), and a Result summary posted only after the Result is shared, with no comments, counts or Discussion guide.

| Need | Slack (Block Kit) | Teams (Adaptive Card) |
| --- | --- | --- |
90→| Plain link | mrkdwn `<url\|text>` in a `section` or `context` block ([formatting text](https://docs.slack.dev/messaging/formatting-message-text/)). `chat.postMessage` takes `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` ([method](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/chat.postMessage/)). | `TextBlock` with `[text](url)`. The Chat SDK's own `link` element renders exactly this (`@chat-adapter/teams` `cards.js`). |
| Button-style link | `button` with `url`. **Still sends `block_actions`** (§3.8), so we do not use it. | `Action.OpenUrl`; Teams requires the target domain in the manifest's `validDomains`, otherwise it shows "URL may lead to untrusted content" ([card actions](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/task-modules-and-cards/cards/cards-actions)). The docs do not describe a bot callback for it (unlike `Action.Submit`/`Action.Execute`); confirm in the spike. |
| Reminder | Same blocks in a new message. | Same card in a new message. |
| Edit/remove links later | `chat.update` and `chat.delete` by `channel` + `ts`. | `PUT`/`DELETE v3/conversations/{id}/activities/{activityId}` (present in `@chat-adapter/teams/api`). |
| Result summary | `section` with `fields`, plain text. | `TextBlock`/`FactSet`; the Chat SDK maps tables to the Adaptive Card `Table`. |
| Slash command (SPEC §5.7) | Supported; needs a Request URL. | The Chat SDK's feature matrix says "Slash commands: No" for Teams ([adapter README](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@chat-adapter/teams)). Team health in Teams needs a bot command or message extension, designed separately. |

Fidelity is not what separates the options: the Chat SDK's card model compiles to the same Block Kit and Adaptive Card JSON we would write by hand, and its `link` element is already the plain-link form. Two limits to check in the spike, neither verified here: the maximum number of actions per Adaptive Card in Teams (five rating `Action.OpenUrl` buttons plus "Open check-in" may hit it, in which case use markdown links in a `TextBlock`), and Teams link-preview behaviour for URLs in plain text messages (a preview fetch carries no fragment, so it is harmless to the token, but it would show a title).

**Why plain links are a privacy requirement, not just a style choice.** A Slack button click sends `block_actions` to `MainWorker`, with the clicking Slack user id and a timestamp. That is a Person-bound, timed event for "opened the rating link on Round R" at the moment of answering, delivered to the Worker that has logs, while ADR 0005 keeps all of that off the Submission path. A plain link produces no event.
100→
### 3.5 Slack app and per-Organization install

- Slack apps are installed by the v2 OAuth flow. The app redirects to `https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize?scope=…&client_id=…&redirect_uri=…&state=…`; Slack redirects back to an HTTPS `redirect_uri` with a code, which the server exchanges at `oauth.v2.access`. The docs say to check the `state` parameter. The response gives `access_token` (bot `xoxb-…`), `bot_user_id`, `team.id` and, for Enterprise Grid org-wide installs, `is_enterprise_install` with a null `team` ([installing with OAuth](https://docs.slack.dev/authentication/installing-with-oauth/), [oauth.v2.access](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/oauth.v2.access)).
- Distribution: a new app can be installed only in its development workspace until an OAuth redirect URL is set and distribution is enabled ([Slack Java SDK guide](https://docs.slack.dev/tools/java-slack-sdk/guides/app-distribution)). Apps can be distributed "in either listed or unlisted fashion" ([distribution](https://docs.slack.dev/app-management/distribution)). **Unlisted distribution needs no Marketplace review**; I found nothing that makes listing mandatory, but I did not read the review policy. Install by a Lead may be blocked by the workspace's app-approval setting, which only the workspace can change.
- Bot scopes for R3: `chat:write` for posting (DM by passing the user id as `channel`, per the `chat.postMessage` docs); `users:read.email` for `users.lookupByEmail` (Tier 3, 50+ per minute) to map a Person's email to a Slack user id ([method](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/methods/users.lookupByEmail/)); `commands` for the slash command. Whether DM-by-user-id also needs `im:write` was not confirmed.
- **Privacy note for the ADR:** `users:read.email` means SurveyBeat sends each Person's email address to Slack to find them. That is a new data flow to a third party and must be stated plainly to members (#295 notes). Look-ups should run once at binding time, not per send.
- Rate limit: about 1 message per second per channel, and "several hundred messages per minute" per workspace (`chat.postMessage` docs). Invitation fan-out for a large Team must go through the existing Queue with per-workspace pacing and retries.
- Per-Organization shape: the "Add to Slack" button is a `MainWorker` route that carries a signed `state` binding the install to the Lead's Organization; the callback stores the token in the Organization Durable Object and writes `slack:<team_id> → organizationId` to D1. One Slack workspace maps to one Organization (D1 key unique), because an inbound slash command carries only `team_id`.
- Slack's manifest has an opt-in `token_management_enabled` setting; with token rotation the `oauth.v2.access` example shows bot tokens that expire (`expires_in: 43200`, a 12-hour lifetime) and come with a `refresh_token`. The ADR should pick off for the first release unless the refresh path is built.
110→
### 3.6 Teams registration, proactive messages, and the tenancy risk

**Registration pieces.** An Entra ID app registration, an Azure Bot resource whose messaging endpoint is a `MainWorker` route, the Teams channel enabled on the bot, and a Teams app package (manifest plus icons) that lists the bot, the personal scope and `validDomains`. Microsoft's Teams CLI can create the app, secret, bot registration and install link in one step (adapter README).

**Tenancy: the open problem.**

- Microsoft's registration page says multi-tenant bot creation "will be deprecated after July 31, 2025": existing multi-tenant bots keep working but new ones cannot be created; use single-tenant or user-assigned managed identity ([Register a bot](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/bot-service-quickstart-registration)). The adapter's own default is `appType: "MultiTenant"`, which is a deprecated mode for a newly created bot.
- SurveyBeat must send to Persons in **many customers' tenants** from one bot. A Microsoft Q&A thread *(secondary)* from an ISV with about 100 tenants says the documented single-tenant model "does not provide the cross-tenant outbound capability" their SaaS needs; the answers (a Microsoft external-staff moderator and an MVP) point to a single-tenant bot distributed as a Teams app that other tenants install, user-assigned managed identity, or the newer Microsoft 365 Agents route, without stating that single-tenant outbound to other tenants works ([Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5896006/request-for-exception-to-provision-new-multi-tenan)). Another thread *(secondary)* says publishing through AppSource is "strongly recommended" for external tenants with a single-tenant bot ([Q&A](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/5882874/clarification-on-multi-tenant-support-for-single-t)).
- **I found no Microsoft document that settles whether one single-tenant bot can mint a token and send proactive messages into customer tenants.** This must be resolved by a spike with two real tenants before the ADR commits to Teams; the fallbacks (a bot registration per customer tenant, or only Teams-installed-by-the-tenant scenarios) change the cost and the install story materially.
120→
**Proactive messages.**

- The bot must be installed for the user in the personal scope; otherwise the create-conversation call fails with 403 `ForbiddenOperationException` ([proactive messages](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoftteams/platform/bots/how-to/conversations/send-proactive-messages)). The page offers two ways to install: proactively through Microsoft Graph, or a custom app policy that installs the app for the organization's users.
- To create the conversation the bot needs `tenantId`, the user's `aadObjectId` or `userId`, and the `serviceUrl`; after creation it posts to the returned `conversationId`. `userId` is unique per bot and user and cannot be reused between bots; `channelId` is global (same page).
- The page says to store the `tenantId` and either the `userId` or `channelId`. The adapter's stored shape is `{ conversationId, serviceUrl, tenantId, teamId?, channelId? }` (`extractTeamsContinuation`).
- For each Invitation the thin sender therefore needs a **conversation reference**: `tenantId`, `userId` (and `aadObjectId`), `serviceUrl`, `conversationId`, and per send an `activityId` for later edits.

**Where the reference lives.**

130→- **Organization Durable Object**, in a `channel_binding` table keyed by Person: `channel`, the platform ids above, and the Slack/Teams message ids of each send. Reasons: it identifies a Person, so it belongs with the Person rows (`people`, email) that already live there; deleting a Person then deletes their bindings in one place; the send path already runs through the Organization object (`SendStore`); and it keeps D1 small.
- **D1** holds only the routing key SPEC §6.2 already names, "Slack and Teams workspace to organization": `teams:<tenantId>` and `slack:<teamId>` → `organizationId`, needed because an inbound webhook knows its tenant before it knows the Organization. No Person, conversation id or message content goes to D1.
- If Teams `serviceUrl` can differ per conversation (the Connector's regional hosts), it must be stored per binding, not per tenant.

### 3.7 Teams Safe Links and the URL fragment

**I could not run this test, and I make no claim about a result.** It needs a Microsoft 365 tenant with a Defender for Office 365 licence, a registered Teams bot, and Teams desktop, web and mobile clients. None is available here.

What Microsoft documents ([Safe Links overview](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/defender-office-365/safe-links-about), updated 2026-10):

140→- Safe Links covers "links in Teams conversations, group chats, or from channels", in Teams desktop, web and mobile.
- For Teams, "URLs in Teams are checked against a list of known malicious links when the protected user clicks the link (time-of-click protection). **URLs aren't rewritten.**" This differs from email, where URLs are rewritten to `*.safelinks.protection.outlook.com` (the existing note `docs/research/email-link-scanners.md`).
- The Built-in protection preset applies Safe Links protection in Teams to every recipient in a tenant with at least one Defender for Office 365 licence.
- "The intermediary page that does Safe Links validation redirects to the target page", which the page mentions when explaining why `SameSite=Strict` cookies may fail after opening a link from Teams.

What it does not say: whether the validation request includes the fragment, whether the intermediary redirect keeps it, or whether links inside a bot's Adaptive Card are treated like links in a typed message. A browser inherits the original fragment across an HTTP 3xx redirect when the `Location` header carries none (RFC 9110 §10.2.2), but the page does not say the intermediary uses a 3xx rather than a script redirect.

Two separate risks follow:

1. **The fragment is lost.** `#t=…` and `&v=…` share one fragment, so the likely failure is that both are lost, not just `&v=`. The issue's fallback ("Open check-in only") still needs the token. If the fragment does not survive, the Teams Invitation has no anonymous-safe handoff to `answer.html`. The Channel ADR must treat that as **blocking for Teams**, not as a degraded mode.
150→2. **The fragment reaches Microsoft.** If the click-time check sends the full URL to Microsoft's service, the Invitation token (ADR 0005 keeps it in the fragment so that no scanner or log ever sees it) is exposed to a third party. Email already has the same unknown; this note adds no evidence either way.

Test plan for the spike: in a Defender-licensed test tenant with Teams protection on, post a bot Adaptive Card whose link is `https://<preview-stage>/a#t=TEST&v=3`; click it from desktop, web and mobile; read `location.hash` on the answer page (it can log nothing but its own hash to the console for the test); repeat with the protection setting off as a control; and repeat with the link in a `TextBlock` and in `Action.OpenUrl`. Expected cost: half a day plus a tenant.

### 3.8 Slack: plain links and `block_actions`

- The Slack interaction docs list `block_actions` as the payload for a "Block Kit interactive component", alongside shortcuts, `view_submission` and `view_closed` ([handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/)).
- A button that has a `url` is still an interactive component: "If you're using url, you'll still receive an interaction payload and will need to send an acknowledgement response" ([button element](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/block-kit/block-elements/button-element/)). **So link buttons do send `block_actions` to our Request URL; plain links do not need to be buttons.** The Chat SDK's `link-button` renders as a `button` with `url` and an `action_id` (`@chat-adapter/slack` `blocks.js`), so it would trigger this; its plain `link` element renders as a `section` with `<url|label>` and does not.
- The Events API `link_shared` event is sent "when a link — matching the registered URL domain your app is setup to track — is posted", not when it is clicked; it also requires a subscription and a registered domain, and apps do not receive it for their own messages ([link_shared](https://docs.slack.dev/reference/events/link_shared/)). SurveyBeat should register no unfurl domain and subscribe to no `link_shared`.
- **What is not stated.** Slack does not publish a sentence of the form "clicking a plain link sends nothing to the app". The conclusion rests on the payload list above. Unfurling is a separate matter: with `unfurl_links` left on, Slack's servers may fetch the URL (they send no fragment); set `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media` to false as #295 requires. A live check costs a few minutes: post a message with five plain links to a dev workspace, subscribe the Request URL to a request log, click each, and confirm zero requests.
160→
## 4. Constraints the Channel ADR must keep

1. **Port, not product.** `ChannelSender` stays in `packages/domain` with no Slack, Teams or Cloudflare imports; Slack and Teams senders live in `packages/cloudflare` (boundary rules, ADR 0008). The domain port speaks Invitation, Reminder and Result summary, not "message" or "thread".
2. **No third-party store, no `Chat` runtime in `MainWorker`.** If a later ADR adopts `chat`, it must also name the `StateAdapter` and show it is Cloudflare-only (the Cloudflare `agents` adapter, or one we write over the Organization Durable Object).
3. **Plain links only, previews off.** No Block Kit buttons (including `url` buttons) and no Adaptive Card `Action.Submit`/`Action.Execute`. Slack: `unfurl_links:false`, `unfurl_media:false`, no `link_shared` subscription. Teams: `Action.OpenUrl` or markdown links only. This keeps every chat click out of `MainWorker`, so no Channel click event carries a Person and a time (ADR 0005, ADR 0007).
4. **Where state lives.** The per-Person binding (Slack user id; Teams `tenantId`, `userId`, `serviceUrl`, `conversationId`), the workspace token (encrypted with a Worker secret, like `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY`), and the sent-message ids for later edits live in the Organization Durable Object. D1 holds only `slack:<teamId>` and `teams:<tenantId>` → `organizationId`. Deleting a Person deletes their bindings. No survey content, Answer or Result in D1.
5. **Zero-Leakage Handoff stays.** Chat Channels deliver Invitations, Reminders and shared Result summaries only. Answers still confirm on `answer.html` through the Submission Worker. Nothing in the Channel path may carry both an Invitation token and an Edit key, and no Channel route is served by the Submission Worker.
6. **The token stays in the fragment, and Teams is gated on proof.** Link shape is unchanged: `…/a#t=<token>[&v=<1–5>]`. Teams ships only after the Safe Links spike (§3.7) shows the fragment survives and is not sent to Microsoft; otherwise the ADR must pick another handoff. ADR 0007's rule that the link only preselects and the answer saves on confirm applies unchanged.
7. **Verify before parse, on every inbound route.** Slack: HMAC-SHA256, 300 s skew, raw body. Teams: the Bot Framework JWT checks in §3.2, including the `serviceUrl` claim, and an allowlist of Connector hosts before any outbound call. Each route is classified in `PrivacyRegistry.ts`.
170→8. **Idempotent, queued sends.** Sends go through the existing Queue and `SendStore` pattern: one send id per Person and Round, retry-safe, with per-workspace pacing for Slack's rate limit and a visible failure state when a Person has no binding (not a silent fall back to a different Channel that the Person did not pick).
9. **Member-visible disclosure.** The ADR should require plain wording that sending an Invitation through Slack or Teams is a third-party data flow, and that Slack lookup uses the Person's email (`users:read.email`).
10. **Slack before Teams, Teams behind two spikes:** the tenancy spike (§3.6) and the Safe Links spike (§3.7). Slash command design for Teams (bot command or message extension) is a separate item.
11. **Edits remove links.** Both platforms support editing a sent message by stored id, which #298 relies on; the binding must therefore keep the Slack `channel` + `ts` and the Teams `conversationId` + `activityId` for each send.
12. **One workspace, one Organization.** Reject installing a Slack workspace or Teams tenant that is already bound to another Organization.

## 5. What I could not verify

- **Teams Safe Links and the fragment.** No tenant, no Defender licence. Only the documentation in §3.7 was read.
- **Teams tenancy.** Whether one single-tenant Azure Bot can send proactive messages into other customers' tenants. Microsoft documentation does not answer it; the evidence is two Q&A threads *(secondary)*.
180→- **Valid-path behaviour of any adapter.** No Slack workspace or Azure Bot was available. I verified bundling, loading and the 401 rejection paths in local workerd, not a verified inbound event or an outbound `postMessage`/`createConversation`.
- **Alchemy deployment.** I used `wrangler` for bundling and local workerd. I did not deploy any of these through Alchemy or run them inside the repository's `MainWorker`.
- **Production startup CPU.** Startup numbers are local, on a shared machine, and varied by up to 4× between runs. Re-measure on a deployed preview stage if the Channel ADR leans on them.
- **Slack:** the exact scope set for opening a DM (`im:write` versus `chat:write` alone); the Marketplace review policy for listing; behaviour of `users.lookupByEmail` for guests and Slack Connect users; and the live "no event on plain link click" check (§3.8).

172→- **Roles and permissions.** Organization-level roles are a fact in the Organization's own data: an admin flag (admin, member). Team-level roles (lead, member, viewer) live there too, because they belong to the domain. Permission checks are one function of (person, action, resource), defined in one place and tested as a table.
- **Audit log.** The system records admin and lead actions, such as changing privacy settings, changing anonymity modes, exporting data, and adding leads, in a store inside SurveyBeat.
- **Billing.** Not in the first release. Design the model so that seats or teams per organization can be counted later.

### 5.7 Integrations and API

- **Slack app and Microsoft Teams app.** Members can answer from the messages. Leads get the results summary in a channel they choose. A slash command or message action shows the team's current health.
- **Public API.** A small, versioned HTTP API, authenticated with organization API keys, that returns results and actions. All privacy rules apply.
180→- **MCP server.** A remote MCP server lets a lead use an AI assistant to ask about their teams' results and manage actions. It enforces the same permissions and privacy thresholds as the web app, because it calls the same domain services.
- **Webhooks.** Webhooks for "round results ready" and "action created or updated".

118→- The question library is shared across the organization. Admins can mark questions as standard, so that every team asking the same question produces comparable data across the organization.
- The pulse editor shows an estimated answer time, and warns when a pulse goes over 7 questions or about 90 seconds.
120→- Optional rotation. A pulse can have a fixed core set of questions plus a rotating set, where each round asks one or two different questions. This covers more topics without making each round longer.
- Cadence uses each member's local time zone. Monday 9:00 means 9:00 for each recipient. A lead can skip a round (for holidays) or pause a pulse.
- Channels are email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams. Each member picks their preferred channel. Email is the fallback for everyone.
- The first question can be answered directly from the message. In email, each rating value is a link that opens the answer page with that value chosen; the answer is saved when the member confirms it there, because email security scanners open every link (ADR 0007). In Slack and Teams, the message has interactive buttons and, where the platform allows it, a modal for the rest.
- Reminders go only to members who have not answered, and there are at most two per round. A member can turn reminders off.
- A shareable link remains available for teams that do not use invitations. A link round cannot compute a response rate and cannot guarantee one answer per person. The UI says so.

### 5.2 Answer: the member experience

- The answer page loads in under one second on a mid-range phone on 4G. It needs no sign-in when opened from an invitation token. It does need sign-in when opened from the shared link, if the organization requires it.

28→| Signature verification and stateless handling in `MainWorker`? | Slack: HMAC-SHA256 with Web Crypto, 5-minute skew, no state. Teams: Microsoft's JWT check, which the stateless subpath does **not** implement; we write it. | §3.2 |
| Does it need Redis or another external store? | The `Chat` constructor requires a `StateAdapter`; official ones are Redis, ioredis, Postgres, memory. Redis and Postgres are third-party stores and break SPEC §6. A DO SQLite `StateAdapter` exists but is Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk`, not part of `vercel/chat`. With thin adapters, **no `StateAdapter` is required.** | §3.3 |
30→| Card fidelity? | Slack Block Kit and Teams Adaptive Cards both carry what R3 needs: rating links, a Reminder, a Result summary, and later edits. Plain-link Invitations are possible on both. | §3.4 |
| Slack app and Teams bot registration and per-Organization OAuth install? | Slack: standard distributed app plus OAuth v2 install per workspace. Teams: Entra app plus Azure Bot plus Teams app package; per-tenant admin install; tenancy model unresolved. | §3.5, §3.6 |
| Teams proactive messages, and where does the conversation reference live? | Needs the bot installed in the Person's personal scope, plus tenant id, user id and service URL. Store the per-Person reference in the **Organization Durable Object**; D1 holds only the tenant-to-Organization routing row. | §3.6 |
| Safe Links and the fragment `#t=…&v=…`? | **Not tested.** Microsoft documents that Teams links are checked at click time and not rewritten, and says nothing about fragments. Treat as unverified and gating for Teams. | §3.7 |
| Slack plain links and `block_actions`? | Slack documents `block_actions` as the payload for Block Kit interactive components, and a URL button still sends one. Plain `<url\|text>` links in message text are not interactive components. **Slack does not state "plain links send nothing" in so many words;** the conclusion follows from its payload list and is a one-click live check. | §3.8 |

I will apply all the edits carefully.

The inaccurate sentences are in §3.4 and §3.8. Constraint 3 already states that plain links produce no chat click events. The §2 table is already accurate.

I will soften the language so it does not present the Slack fact as proven. Constraint 3 is a design requirement, not a confirmed claim.

I will add a SPEC reconciliation note after constraint 3. It will cite the Channel ADR and require a SPEC edit to resolve the discrepancy.

SPEC §5.1 and §5.7 still describe interactive buttons and modals, which conflict with the plain-link requirement. AGENTS.md requires recording such contradictions rather than leaving them silent. Constraint 6 also needs narrowing to clarify the Safe Links gate.

The Safe Links spike only confirms the fragment survives to the answer page. It does not prove Microsoft's click-time check receives the token. This exposure remains an open question for the ADR. The test plan will be updated to reflect that the hash read only shows survival. Risk 2 stays as a separate risk that the spike does not close.

The §2 table Safe Links row will be tightened to clarify the gate is fragment survival, not proof Microsoft never sees the token.

Q&A 5882874 needs a proactive token rejection sentence.

Q&A 5896006 attribution needs correction. The workaround list comes from two moderators, but the MVP answer wrongly claims only Microsoft can grant an exception. The Microsoft 365 Agent / Copilot extensibility mention is present, yet its author was never confirmed.

The `extractTeamsContinuation` schema will include `conversationId`, `serviceUrl`, and optional `tenantId`, `teamId`, `channelId`, `activityId`, and `replyToId`.

The allowlist will add `smba.infra.gov.teams.microsoft.us`.

The `people` table will be renamed to `person` in `0003_person.sql`.

`tenant-isolated` will be renamed to `Organization-isolated`.

The AGENTS.md citation will require the Channel ADR to name the exact package version when reusing Ratstack templates.

Bot Framework requirements 4 and 6 correspond to audience and signature. Constraint 7 still requires every check, including serviceUrl. The Safe Links table and §5 unverified note will be updated to reflect this.

I will edit PR 318 now while no ports are in use. I will start the 317 commit monitor only after 317's gate is complete, to avoid a race condition. The 317 script commits when ports are free, so starting both watchers at once could collide. I will commit 318 only after 317 finishes.

details.context_before:
1. **Slack first**, as #295 sequences it. About five endpoints are needed: signature verification (Web Crypto HMAC), `oauth.v2.access`, `chat.postMessage`, `chat.update`/`chat.delete`, and `users.lookupByEmail`. All are plain `fetch` calls validated with Effect Schema at the boundary.
2. **Teams second, behind a tenancy spike** (§3.6). The Azure Bot tenancy rules changed in 2025 and a single-tenant bot may not reach other customers' tenants. This is the largest unresolved risk in R3.
3. **No external store, no `StateAdapter`.** Everything an outbound-first Channel needs (installation token, Person-to-Channel binding, sent-message id for later edits) is Organization state and belongs in the Organization Durable Object beside the existing `SendStore`. Redis would break SPEC §6; the Durable Object SQLite `StateAdapter` that exists today ships in Cloudflare's `agents` package, not in `vercel/chat` (§3.3), and is not worth taking on for a surface this narrow.
details.context_after: **Revisit this if** a later release wants in-chat conversation (threads, "reply to answer", streaming). Then `chat` plus Cloudflare's `agents/chat-sdk` state adapter is the route to evaluate, and #295's exclusion of in-chat Answer submission would need its own ADR.
details.line_prefix: 4. **Treat `@chat-adapter/{slack,teams}` as reference and test vectors**, not as a dependency. Their stateless subpath modules (`/webhook`, `/api`, `/blocks`, `/cards`) are small, MIT, `fetch`-based and run in workerd with 13.1 KiB gzip (*measured*). Our code is smaller than the cost of tracking a package that shipped seven minor releases between 2026-08-14 and 2026-11-13.

Its list is the Bearer header, the JWT, the issuer, the audience, validity, the signature, and the `serviceUrl` claim, so 4 and 6 are audience and signature. The `serviceUrl` claim is item 7. details.new_string: The page says "All of these requirements are important, particularly requirements 4 and 6" ([Bot Connector authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication)). Its list is the Bearer header, the JWT, the issuer, the audience, validity, the signature, and the `serviceUrl` claim, so 4 and 6 are audience and signature. The `serviceUrl` claim is item 7. Constraint 7 still requires every check, including `serviceUrl`.
details.context_before: **Slack.** Requests carry `x-slack-request-timestamp` and `x-slack-signature`; the adapter verifies `v0=` + HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:<timestamp>:<body>` with `crypto.subtle`, and rejects a timestamp more than 300 s off (`@chat-adapter/slack@4.45.0`, `dist/chunk-KYABMAGK.js`). This is stateless and about 40 lines in Effect with Web Crypto. Slack must receive an acknowledgement within 3 seconds for interaction payloads ([handling user interaction](https://docs.slack.dev/interactivity/handling-user-interaction/)); a slash command should ack immediately and post the answer through `response_url`, which accepts up to 5 posts within 30 minutes (same page). `MainWorker` must read the raw body once and verify before parsing.
details.context_after: **Useful guard to copy from the Teams adapter:** it refuses to send a bot token to any `serviceUrl` outside an allowlist (`smba.trafficmanager.net` and the GCC, DoD and China hosts) or a loopback emulator (`dist/chunk-4NNW2LU4.js`). `serviceUrl` arrives in the inbound activity, so an unchecked value is a token-exfiltration path.
details.line_prefix: **Teams.** Microsoft requires the bot to verify a JWT on every inbound request: `Authorization: Bearer`, issuer `https://api.botframework.com`, audience equal to the bot's app id, within validity (5-minute skew), RS256 signature from the keys at `https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/keys`, and a `serviceUrl` claim equal to the activity's `serviceUrl`.

details.old_string: it refuses to send a bot token to any `serviceUrl` outside an allowlist (`smba.trafficmanager.net` and the GCC, DoD and China hosts) or a loopback emulator (`dist/chunk-4NNW2LU4.js`).
details.new_string: it refuses to send a bot token to any `serviceUrl` outside an allowlist (`smba.trafficmanager.net`, the government host `smba.infra.gov.teams.microsoft.us`, and the GCC, DoD and China hosts) or a loopback emulator (`dist/chunk-4NNW2LU4.js`).
details.context_before: **Teams.** Microsoft requires the bot to verify a JWT on every inbound request: `Authorization: Bearer`, issuer `https://api.botframework.com`, audience equal to the bot's app id, within validity (5-minute skew), RS256 signature from the keys at `https://login.botframework.com/v1/.well-known/keys`, and a `serviceUrl` claim equal to the activity's `serviceUrl`. The page says "All of these requirements are important, particularly requirements 4 and 6" ([Bot Connector authentication](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/bot-service/rest-api/bot-framework-rest-connector-authentication)). Its list is the Bearer header, the JWT, the issuer, the audience, validity, the signature, and the `serviceUrl` claim, so 4 and 6 are audience and signature. The `serviceUrl` claim is item 7. Constraint 7 still requires every check, including `serviceUrl`. The stateless `@chat-adapter/teams/webhook` subpath **only parses** activities; it contains no JWT, JWKS or OpenID code (grep of the 4.45.0 `dist`). JWT verification lives in the heavy `@microsoft/teams.apps` path. So the thin route has to write this check either way. It needs `crypto.subtle` RS256 verify, a cached JWKS fetch, and the `serviceUrl` claim match. The single-tenant variant (tenant-specific issuer and metadata) was not confirmed from documentation; see §5.
details.context_after: **Where it runs.** Both verifications are request-local and stateless, so they can sit in `MainWorker` beside the Better Auth routes, with each route's classification added to `packages/api/src/PrivacyRegistry.ts`. The Submission Worker stays untouched; no Channel traffic may reach it (ADR 0005).
