155→- Leave out `user`, `session_id`, `metadata`, `trace` and the `x-session-id` header. Each one sends an identifier upstream or into OpenRouter's observability.
- If the spike shows `data_collection: "deny"` rejects Meta, drop it and rely on the account-level "no training" privacy setting plus `only` and `allow_fallbacks: false`. Record that in the ADR.
- If the ADR requires real no-retention, add `"zdr": true`. The call will fail with this model, so the ADR then needs another model.
- Account settings to set and record: Input & Output Logging off, "OpenRouter Use of Inputs/Outputs" off, training providers excluded for paid models. Use a dedicated API key with a guardrail that allows only `meta/muse-ember` and has a small budget.

160→## 8. In-region routing

Sources: <https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/in-region-routing.md>, <https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/features/sovereign-ai.md>, the model page.

- EU in-region routing (`https://eu.openrouter.ai`) is on Business and Enterprise plans. The request is "routed only to shared provider endpoints in that region", and "If no endpoint eligible for the region … can serve the request, it errors instead of leaving the region".
- Muse Ember: "Not currently available through EU in-region routing" (model page). `GET /api/v1/models?region=eu` returned 69 models, none of them Muse. `?region=us` returned 134, with `meta/muse-glimmer-30b` but not Muse Ember. **Muse Ember has no regional guarantee in either region.**
- Even on `eu.openrouter.ai`, "Account and operational records" and "Abuse-monitoring metadata" may be stored or processed in the US.

## 9. DPA

170→Sources: <https://openrouter.ai/data-processing-agreement> (last updated 2026-08-26), <https://openrouter.ai/terms> §10.2.

- **Yes, and it applies by default.** Terms §10.2: for organizations or commercial use, "The DPA is incorporated by reference into, and made a part of, these Terms." No separate signature is needed.
- The customer is Controller and OpenRouter is Processor (§2.1). EEA transfers use Module 2 SCCs, Irish law and Dublin courts (§13.2). There is a UK Addendum and Swiss terms. Breach notice within 72 hours. Deletion of Customer Data on request within 30 business days.
- §2.2: "Customer is responsible for reviewing the data handling terms set forth in AI Model Terms and configuring Customer's account accordingly." **Meta's retention is the customer's problem under the DPA, not OpenRouter's.**
- §5.2: subprocessor-change notices exclude "processing by AI Model Providers". Model providers can change without the 30-day notice.
- **Exhibit A (EU-only processing)** applies only when elected in an Order Form or other written agreement, and only for traffic through the EU API, which routes only to EU Model Providers. It cannot cover Muse Ember, which has no EU endpoint.
- Schedule 1 says "No processing of Sensitive Data or any special categories is intended". Survey comments about a workplace can contain special-category data (health, union membership), and redaction does not remove it.

## 10. Calling from a Worker or Durable Object
180→
Sources: [Workers limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/platform/limits/), [Workers secrets](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/secrets/), OpenRouter [errors](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/errors-and-debugging.md) and [limits](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits.md).

- **Transport.** Plain `fetch("https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions", { method: "POST", headers: { Authorization: "Bearer " + key, "Content-Type": "application/json" }, body })`. No SDK is needed. The optional `HTTP-Referer` and `X-Title` headers are for attribution only and should be left out.
- **Secret.** Store `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` as a Worker secret, declared in `infra/alchemy.run.ts`, and read it from `env`. Only the Worker or Durable Object that runs the theming job gets the binding, never the Submission Worker.
- **CPU and duration.** "Waiting on network requests (such as `fetch()` calls …) does **not** count toward CPU time". Paid CPU defaults to 30 s per request. "There is no hard limit on duration for HTTP-triggered Workers" while the client stays connected. Alarms have 15 min of wall time (see `durable-objects-workflows-limits.md`). Run the call from a Durable Object alarm or a Workflow step, not from the Lead's HTTP request.
- **Timeouts.** OpenRouter documents no server-side request timeout beyond the `408` code. Set your own: `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(60_000)` is generous against a p99 of 5.9 s to first token plus a few thousand reasoning tokens at p99 throughput (18 tokens/s, so about 4 minutes in the worst case). Measure in the spike. Note `isAbortable: false` on Meta's provider record: an aborted request may still run, and may still be billed, upstream.
- **Errors.** A request error has an HTTP status equal to `error.code`. Errors after the model starts can arrive with HTTP **200** and an `error` in the body, so always check the body. Retry `408`, `429`, `502` and `503` with exponential backoff and jitter, honouring `Retry-After` on 429/503. Do not retry `400`, `401`, `402` or `403` (`403` covers moderation flags and budget blocks). Do not retry `finish_reason: "length"` with the same budget. A Workflow step's built-in `retries` (5, exponential) fits.
- **Rate limits.** OpenRouter's published request caps are for `:free` models and key management only. Paid model capacity is "govern[ed] … globally". One call per Round is far below any of them.
- **Logging.** The theming code must not log request bodies, response bodies or error bodies (moderation errors echo up to 100 characters of input). Log the status code, `error.code`, token counts from `usage`, and duration only.
190→
## 11. Where the sources are silent

- Which Meta tier (Standard or Contributor) Muse Ember traffic from OpenRouter uses, and whether OpenRouter has a separate agreement with Meta.
- Where Meta processes requests (country or data centre).

- "OpenRouter does not store your prompts or responses, *unless* you opt in" to **Private Input & Output Logging** or **OpenRouter Use of Inputs/Outputs** (the 1% discount), "or content is flagged as potential CSAM". Both opt-ins are off by default. Keep them off, and check both settings in every workspace.

Flagged content "may be retained for human review, reporting, and preservation where required by law". Reported material is preserved for one year under 18 U.S.C. § 2258A. For text-only comment theming this is unlikely to trigger, but it is one more documented reason prompts can be kept.

5. **What members must be told,** on the answer page and the privacy page, before they write: that comments are sent, after the listed redaction, to Meta through OpenRouter (both US companies) to group them into themes; that Meta keeps them for up to 30 days and may keep flagged content longer; that neither uses them for training (subject to risk 2); that processing is not limited to the EU; and that OpenRouter screens requests for CSAM. The current answer-page sentence "Your name is never stored with your answers" stays true, but it is no longer the whole story for comments.

matches.content: The landing page (`SiteWorker`, ADR 0020) uses the stage's own name without `app` or `submit`: `pr-<n>.surveybeat.app` and `staging.surveybeat.app`. `production` serves it on workers.dev until the apex cutover below, and every other stage stays on workers.dev. On a stage without an `app` hostname (personal `dev-*` stages), the page's sign-in links (`/app`) cannot know the app's workers.dev URL and lead back to the landing page; open `mainUrl` from the deploy output instead.

`surveybeat.app` and `www.surveybeat.app` still point at the old app on Vercel, and production deploys on every merge to main. Do these steps in this order, or the production deploy collides with the old records:
3. Merge to main. The production deploy claims the apex.

| `production` | Sends through Cloudflare Email Sending from `team@notify.surveybeat.app` | The `notify.surveybeat.app` sending subdomain, the `send_email` binding, the `EmailEvents` queue, and its event subscription |

No stage other than `production` can send real mail. To try real sending elsewhere, change `sendsRealEmail` in `packages/cloudflare/src/Email.ts` on a throwaway branch and deploy a personal stage. That stage then also claims `notify.surveybeat.app` and its event subscription, so destroy it before production is deployed.

**The `send_email` binding is named `SendEmail`.** Binding names share one namespace per Worker. Until #147 it was named `Email`, like the Email queue's producer binding; the deploy kept only the queue, so production queued each rendered email instead of sending it and every send failed as `unknown`. Read the deployed bindings back with `cf workers versions get <version> --worker-id <main worker>` when email stops arriving.

- **Queues.** `Jobs`/`JobsDlq` carry the Organization's scheduled work, `Email`/`EmailDlq` the transactional sends, and `EmailEvents` the bounce and complaint subscription (production only). Cloudflare neither drains nor alerts on a dead-letter queue, which is why each has its own consumer, and the email queue keeps 10 attempts.

- **Email retention.** The sending subdomain is declared with `previewEnabled: false`, so Cloudflare does not keep each message, invitation links included, for about a week. Only `production` binds `send_email`; every other stage records into `captured_email`.

POSTs with an `Origin` other than the stage's own are refused (`requireSameOrigin`), and Better Auth's own endpoints check `trustedOrigins`.

1→# Infrastructure: Alchemy stack and preview stages

The stack is `infra/alchemy.run.ts` (stack name `Surveybeat`). Run Alchemy from the repository root, because the Durable Object's SQL migrations are found relative to the working directory.

| Stage | Hostnames |
| --- | --- |
| `pr-<n>` | `pr-<n>.dashboard.surveybeat.app`, `pr-<n>.submit.surveybeat.app` |
| `staging` | `staging.dashboard.surveybeat.app`, `staging.submit.surveybeat.app` |
| `production` | `dashboard.surveybeat.app`, `submit.surveybeat.app` (with `app.surveybeat.app` redirecting to `dashboard`) |
10→| any other (personal dev, tests) | workers.dev |

A new custom hostname takes about a minute to get its certificate, so the first requests fail the TLS handshake. `infra/scripts/smoke.ts` retries.

The landing page (`SiteWorker`, ADR 0020) uses the stage's own name without `app` or `submit`: `pr-<n>.surveybeat.app` and `staging.surveybeat.app`. `production` serves it on workers.dev until the apex cutover below, and every other stage stays on workers.dev. On a stage without an `app` hostname (personal `dev-*` stages), the page's sign-in links (`/app`) cannot know the app's workers.dev URL and lead back to the landing page; open `mainUrl` from the deploy output instead.

docs/infra.md line 69 states AI features fail closed when unset and return empty otherwise.

Rotation of a non-empty key does not fail closed. The runbook should instruct removing or emptying the secret. ADR 0022 and docs/infra.md conflict on BETTER_AUTH_SECRET: the former says the Alchemy BetterAuth resource provisions its own signing secret, while the latter treats it as a non-stage secret from authOptions.

Checking the secrets section in alchemy.run.ts.

The secret originates from a BetterAuth resource.

The runbook should instruct revoking affected `auth_session` rows. `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is not a dashboard stage secret; the Alchemy `BetterAuth` resource provisions it. Replacing it would sign everyone out. I will write targeted search_replace edits on the 321 worktree files.

Drafting exact replacements for ropa.md. The C-3 purpose cell will use "Persons" instead of "users". The P-3 personal data cell will be updated with a specific phrase. Comments in markdown docs are not subject to code comment lint.

The P-3 personal data cell will specify `StoredEmail` JSON in `email_send.content` rather than rendered HTML. Invitation and reminder rows store an `InvitationRef` with `roundId`, `personId`, and `generation`; the token is derived when the Queue consumer renders the message. Legacy `InvitationEmailWithToken` or `ReminderEmailWithToken` rows may still hold a raw token. Non-production D1 `captured_email` stores rendered `subject`, `html`, and `text`. Provider `message_id` and delivery, bounce, and complaint codes are also included. The P-4 retention section is next.

P-4 retention will state that active Person data is kept for the "My history" Round list and deleted immediately when a Person is removed from the directory. It will also note that Round data is deleted when a Round is cancelled.

P-5 will qualify team members as non-personal once stored. The updated text notes that stored rows contain no Person column, though a comment can still identify its author through a unique anecdote.

P-5 localStorage will list `sb_edit_<roundId>` and `sb_answers_<roundId>` as client-only keys. The retention note will state that submission and answer rows survive Person removal, and that cancelling a Round deletes its answer, submission, and participation rows.

P-5 retention will also note that the `sb_answers_<roundId>` localStorage key expires after one year.

P-6 will state that Results are computed only when the Minimum group size is met. The payload must not include Person IDs, emails, Team or Organization names, or timestamps. Question text is the author's string and must not contain personal data. Comment text is redacted before storage; name redaction uses email local parts because the Person table has no display-name column.

Section 3 item 2 will note that invitation tokens travel in the URL fragment for answer links, but GET /delivery?token= and GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe?t= still send them in the query string, exposing them to Workers Logs and Referer.

Section 3 item 3 will state that `recordFirstAnswer` and `saveAnswer` call the `redact` function on the Organization Durable Object before writing to SQLite. `SubmissionWorker` forwards raw answers over Durable Object RPC and does not redact them itself.

The roster passed to redact is the directory's PersonRecord list, which contains email but no display name. Redaction strips email local parts, email addresses, phone numbers, @handles, and URLs, replacing them with [name], [email], [phone], [handle], and [link]. A display name that is not part of an email local part is not removed.

The Section 3 introduction will be qualified to note that the anonymous submission and answer tables are engineered and test-verified to satisfy Recital 26 anonymization at rest and in normal operation.

The Section 3 introduction will state that stored rows contain no Person identifier column. This structural split is test-verified. It is not a claim that every stored comment is non-personal. Comments that identify their author through unique anecdotes are personal data for retention and rights requests. The survival bullet about non-personal statistical data also needs qualification.

The residual caveat will cite `apps/web/src/messages/answer.ts` instead of `catalog.ts` for the answer page disclosure.

The in-app Privacy page uses a separate `privacy.comments.body` in `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts`.

Line 85 will change from `as of commit 2a58b095` to `in the current tree`.

`dpia.md` line 20 will read `if Submissions could be attributed to individuals` instead of `responses`.

Line 30 will read `and calls redact (Redaction.ts) on each comment before inserting into answer.`

Line 32 will read `sends stored comment text (redacted at store time), each Question's text, dimension, score, and change, Dimension scores and changes, and redacted titles of open Actions. Question text is not redacted.`

Lines 45-46 will be rewritten as a transparency paragraph.

The R-01 mitigation section is next.

R-01 will state that submission and answer tables are WITHOUT ROWID, use random 128-bit IDs, and contain no person, invitation, time, or locale columns. Participation is a separate table keyed by round_id and person_id, structurally distinct from submission with no shared key or timestamp. The R-01 mitigation will also note that invitation tokens travel in the URL fragment, with answer links using the #t= fragment.

R-04 will change "A respondent names a colleague" to "A Team member names a colleague". The redaction step will be specified as running in the Organization Durable Object (SqlRounds.ts) before the SQLite insert, after SubmissionWorker forwards the raw answers. It replaces email local parts from the directory roster, emails, phone numbers, @handles, and URLs.

R-05 will state that only RedactedText comments, Question text, Dimension scores and changes, and redacted open Action titles are sent. Person IDs, names, and emails are never included.

R-05 will also state that the payload excludes timestamps. R-07 will specify that one-tap answer links pass the Invitation token in the URL fragment as `#t=`.

The residual risk will be Medium until issue #311 removes query-string tokens, because that path is live. The fragment path alone would be Low. Evidence will cite PageRoutes.ts and issue #311. The breach runbook replacements are next.

The breach runbook decision tree is being restructured. A new node R will handle the processor-only path when the risk to rights and freedoms is unlikely. This preserves the existing Q node for post-incident remediation. The K branch will split into an unlikely-risk path to R and a likely-risk path to Q.

The breach runbook checklist is the real delay. It forces a T+24–T+48 window that can stall individual notification when high risk is obvious during triage. The tree node O is not time-boxed. The checklist rows will be tightened. The K branch also needs a "No" path.

The vendor register will add a caveat that OpenRouter retains content flagged as potential CSAM, including ZDR traffic. The Cloudflare row will note that its non-personal claim is subject to the free-text caveat in ropa.md §3.

P-6's shuffled redacted comments are acceptable. The retention sentence will cite both catalog.ts and history.intro. Markdown tables may be long, but that is existing style. Edits will be applied now. The pre-commit gate must be free before committing. The implementer will edit the files directly because the wording involves judgment.

GitHub replies will be posted after the commit is pushed, with attribution and SHA citation. The 14 threads include CodeRabbit comments that require replies, but the Neon review and walkthrough are informational and do not need replies.

The decision tree will use the exact mermaid block. The checklist will add a sentence to the T+2–T+6 window and adjust the T+24–T+48 window. Production canary commands must not include actual token values.

The production preview-privacy test requires `--stage production` with both the dashboard and submission URLs. The observability verification line will be updated to include these arguments. The Internal Breach Register reference will be corrected from §7.4 to §6.4. The EMAIL_DEAD_LETTERED sentence also needs revision. Files will be written in batches using search_replace.

P-5's legal basis column will be qualified. The vendor register row will state that ingestion is the Controller's Art. 6 basis, stored rows contain no Person column, and comments identifying their author remain personal data.

The OpenRouter vendor row will be tightened to list only stored comment text, Question text, dimension scores and changes, and redacted open Action titles. Person IDs, names, emails, and timestamps will be excluded.

The OpenRouter vendor row will clarify that name redaction uses email local parts, and that the person table has no display-name column per ropa.md §4. The LIA line 63 customer instruction will be corrected to prevent copying a false zero-prompt retention claim.

The LIA customer instruction will be rewritten to state that if AI processing is enabled, the payload includes stored comment text, unredacted Question text, scores and changes, and redacted open Action titles sent via OpenRouter to EU ZDR endpoints with zdr: true.

The OpenRouter vendor row will cite docs/research/openrouter-muse-ember.md §6, noting that reported material is retained for one year. The LIA line 61 will be rewritten to state that redact removes email addresses, phone numbers, @handles, URLs, and email local parts from the Organization roster before a comment is stored.

LIA line 71 will be rewritten to require the Invitation to state the Minimum group size and that the name is not stored with the answers, citing packages/emails/src/messages/catalog.ts.

LIA line 72 will be rewritten to state that a person can remove their record with directory.removePerson.

The LIA line 72 rewrite will note that removing a person sets person.removed_at and membership.ended_at, deletes person_index, participation, and test_send rows, and revokes Invitations. The person row and membership history remain; no automated purge removes them.

The unsubscribe path will change from `/unsubscribe` to `/api/reminders/unsubscribe`. This same correction applies to dpia line 46 and the vendor register line 72.

The Google and AWS vendor rows both claim "zero prompt/output retention under ZDR". A short clause will be added to both.

dpia R-04 will replace "user notice" with "answer-page disclosure" in the residual column to avoid glossary terminology. infra.md already includes the required arguments and needs no change. I will now apply all replacements, matching exact long table-cell strings. I will also check whether "threshold" appears elsewhere in the flagged documents.

The remaining flagged documents are now identified: ropa P-6, dpia lines 20 and 59, and vendor non-responders. The mermaid decision tree is being finalized so that the K node's No branch is reachable from the processor path when controller data is unaffected.

The processor-only path is safe because the No branch still lands in the register. Node R correctly assigns the Art. 34 assessment to the customer. The checklist will be tightened so that if high risk to individuals is already apparent during triage, the Art. 34 assessment starts immediately rather than waiting until T+24. This will be added to the T+2h–T+6h row and the T+24h–T+48h window will be softened.

The T+2–T+6 checklist row now explicitly requires starting the Art. 34 assessment immediately when high risk to individuals is already apparent. The T+24–T+48 window will finish any assessment that was not started during triage. The T+72h row already covers issuing the Art. 34 report.

The OpenRouter containment procedure is being drafted. It requires removing or emptying the `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` on the Worker. `OpenRouterAiClient` returns `AiNotConfigured` only when the key is missing or empty. A rotated non-empty key would keep sending data. Organizations with `ai_processing = 1` must be notified.

The OpenRouter containment procedure now includes two additional key rotations. The `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY` requires rotating the Alchemy secret, revoking unredeemed invitations in the affected Organization Durable Objects, and purging stale `invitation_index` rows. Edit keys are generated randomly in the browser and stored only as SHA-256 hashes, so no server secret exists to rotate; a leaked key can alter a Submission while the Round is open, requiring the Round to be closed or the browser to clear `sb_edit_<roundId>`.

The session compromise containment procedure now requires deleting affected auth_session rows in D1 and forcing re-authentication. BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is not a stage secret that operators rotate in the dashboard; the Alchemy BetterAuth resource provisions the signing secret, so replacing that resource signs every session out and should only be done when the signing secret itself is compromised. The bare `pnpm test:preview-privacy` sentence in section 2 will be replaced with the full canary command.

Using unique substrings for replacements. Updating the persons routing label, email content wording, the hard-deletion sentence, and the storage key names.

content.newText: When enabled: (1) the payload is stored comment text, `Question` text, each `Question`'s dimension, score, and change, `Dimension` scores and changes, and redacted open `Action` titles (`buildThemesInput`). It does not include `Person` IDs, emails, `Team` or `Organization` names, or timestamps. `Question` text is not redacted, so a name typed into a `Question` is sent. Comment name redaction uses email local parts, not a display-name column. (2) `OpenRouterAiClient.ts` pins `provider.zdr: true`, `only: ["google-vertex/europe", "amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1"]`, `allow_fallbacks: false`, `data_collection: "deny"`. It returns `AiNotConfigured` only when `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is missing or empty; a non-empty rotated key still sends. (3) OpenRouter account prompt/output logging and training opt-ins are disabled. (4) Response and error bodies (for example moderation `403` echoes) are never logged. (5) `Comment theme`s require `>= 2` supporting comments and pass a 6-word anti-quote check. *(Caveat: upstream ZDR is not "OpenRouter keeps nothing". OpenRouter may retain content flagged as potential CSAM, including ZDR traffic; reported material is kept for one year under 18 U.S.C. § 2258A. Account and abuse metadata can be processed in the US. See `docs/research/openrouter-muse-ember.md` §6.)*

| **R-04** | **Free-text PII and third-party naming in comments.** A `Team` member names a colleague, enters an email, phone, handle, or URL, or leaves identifying context. | High × Medium (**High**) | **ADR 0009:** Synchronous rule-based `redact` (`Redaction.ts`) runs in the `Organization` Durable Object (`SqlRounds.ts`) before the SQLite insert, after `SubmissionWorker` has forwarded the raw answers. It replaces email local parts from the directory roster (`person` stores email and no display name), emails, phone numbers, `@handles`, and URLs with placeholders. Raw text is never stored or logged. `Lead`s cannot link comments to ratings or `Submission` order. *(Limitation: a display name that is not in an email local part, a nickname, or a unique anecdote is not removed. The answer page says so.)* | `Redaction.privacy.test.ts`, `Submissions.privacy.test.ts` (A4b), `answer.ts` (`answer.comment.disclosure`). | **Medium** *(the answer-page disclosure says what is left in, and themes are a further abstraction)* |
| **R-05** | **Free-text PII leakage, prompt retention, or cross-border transfer to AI sub-processors.** Comments sent to an LLM are logged, retained for 30 days, trained on, or routed outside the EEA. | High × High (**Critical**) | **ADR 0015, ADR 0016, ADR 0019:** `organization.ai_processing` defaults to `0` (off). When enabled: (1) the payload is stored comment text, `Question` text, each `Question`'s dimension, score, and change, `Dimension` scores and changes, and redacted open `Action` titles (`buildThemesInput`). It does not include `Person` IDs, emails, `Team` or `Organization` names, or timestamps. `Question` text is not redacted, so a name typed into a `Question` is sent. Comment name redaction uses email local parts, not a display-name column. (2) `OpenRouterAiClient.ts` pins `provider.zdr: true`, `only: ["google-vertex/europe", "amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1"]`, `allow_fallbacks: false`, `data_collection: "deny"`. It returns `AiNotConfigured` only when `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is missing or empty; a non-empty rotated key still sends. (3) OpenRouter account prompt/output logging and training opt-ins are disabled. (4) Response and error bodies (for example moderation `403` echoes) are never logged. (5) `Comment theme`s require `>= 2` supporting comments and pass a 6-word anti-quote check. *(Caveat: upstream ZDR is not "OpenRouter keeps nothing". OpenRouter may retain content flagged as potential CSAM, including ZDR traffic; reported material is kept for one year under 18 U.S.C. § 2258A. Account and abuse metadata can be processed in the US. See `docs/research/openrouter-muse-ember.md` §6.)* | `OpenRouterAiClient.test.ts`, `Themes.privacy.test.ts`, `0011_ai_processing.sql`. | **Low–Medium** |
| **R-06** | **Point-in-time restore (PITR) correlation attack.** Restoring a Durable Object to a prior timestamp replays transaction order, correlating a `participation` insert with its `submission`. | Low × High (**Medium**) | **ADR 0005:** Explicitly excluded from the cryptographic at-rest guarantee. Mitigated by restricting PITR restores exclusively to named, credentialed infrastructure operators (zero access for `Organization admin`s or `Lead`s), strict **30-day** backup expiry (`Policy.backupRetentionDays = 30`), and plain-language disclosure on the `Privacy` page (`catalog.ts` `privacy.restore`, `privacy.restoreTrigger`). | `Policy.ts`, `catalog.ts`, `docs/adr/0005-anonymous-submission-storage.md`. | **Low** |

- **`Invitation` token key (`INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY`):** Rotate the Alchemy secret, revoke unredeemed `invitation`s in the affected `Organization` Durable Objects, and purge stale `invitation_index` rows. This key derives `Invitation` and test-`Invitation` tokens only.
- **`Edit key` exposure:** An `Edit key` is a random value generated in the browser (`apps/web/src/answer/main.ts`) and the server stores only its SHA-256 hash. There is no server secret to rotate, and rotating `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY` does not invalidate `Edit key`s. A leaked browser key (`sb_edit_<roundId>`) can change that `Submission` while the `Round` is open. Close the `Round`, or clear that browser key.

A rotated non-empty key keeps sending. Notify `Organization`s with `ai_processing = 1`.

| **Data Controller** (Art. 34) | Controller-scope breach **likely to result in a high risk** to the rights and freedoms of natural persons (unless Art. 34(3) exemptions apply, e.g., strong encryption with uncompromised keys). | **Without undue delay** after triage confirms high risk. | Affected individuals (`Person`s / sign-in account holders), in clear and plain language. |

- **`SubmissionWorker` logging/traces enabled:** Immediately redeploy `SubmissionWorker` via `pnpm infra:deploy --stage production` (or patch script settings via Cloudflare API) and verify `pnpm check:observability --stage production` and `pnpm test:preview-privacy` pass; audit Cloudflare Workers Logs retention window for any captured payloads.
- **Session / Auth compromise (`auth_session`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`):** Revoke affected `auth_session` rows in D1 (which cascades `auth_session_organization`), rotate `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, and force re-authentication.
- **`Invitation` / `Edit key` secret compromise (`INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY`):** Rotate `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY` in Alchemy/Cloudflare secrets, revoke unredeemed `invitation`s in affected `Organization` DOs, and purge stale `invitation_index` rows.
- **AI sub-processor incident (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` / EU ZDR breach):** Revoke/rotate `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` in Cloudflare Worker secrets (which causes `OpenRouterAiClient` to fail closed with `AiNotConfigured` immediately—zero further calls leave the DO), and notify affected `Organization`s with `ai_processing = 1`.
content.newText:
- **`SubmissionWorker` logging/traces enabled:** Immediately redeploy `SubmissionWorker` via `pnpm infra:deploy --stage production` (or patch script settings via Cloudflare API). Then verify `pnpm check:observability --stage production` and `pnpm test:preview-privacy --stage production https://dashboard.surveybeat.app https://submit.surveybeat.app` (with `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` and `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` set). Audit the Cloudflare Workers Logs retention window for any captured payloads.
- **Session compromise (`auth_session`):** Delete the affected `auth_session` rows in D1 (that cascades `auth_session_organization`) and force re-authentication. `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` is not a stage secret an operator rotates in the dashboard. The Alchemy `BetterAuth` resource provisions the signing secret (ADR 0022, `docs/infra.md`). Replace that resource only when the signing secret itself is compromised; that signs every session out.
- **`Invitation` token key (`INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY`):** Rotate the Alchemy secret, revoke unredeemed `invitation`s in the affected `Organization` Durable Objects, and purge stale `invitation_index` rows. This key derives `Invitation` and test-`Invitation` tokens only.
- **`Edit key` exposure:** An `Edit key` is a random value generated in the browser (`apps/web/src/answer/main.ts`) and the server stores only its SHA-256 hash. There is no server secret to rotate, and rotating `INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY` does not invalidate `Edit key`s. A leaked browser key (`sb_edit_<roundId>`) can change that `Submission` while the `Round` is open. Close the `Round`, or clear that browser key.
- **AI sub-processor incident (`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` / EU ZDR breach):** Remove or empty `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` on the Worker. `OpenRouterAiClient` returns `AiNotConfigured` only when the key is missing or `""` (`OpenRouterAiClient.ts`). A rotated non-empty key keeps sending. Notify `Organization`s with `ai_processing = 1`.

60→### 4.1 Decision Tree

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Signal detected (canary-sweep, check:observability, OPERATOR_ALERT, Cloudflare/OpenRouter advisory, report)"] --> B["T+0h: Contain & preserve evidence"]
    B --> C{"Confirmed security incident affecting confidentiality, integrity, or availability?"}
    C -- No --> D["Close as false positive / operational defect; document"]
    C -- Yes --> E{"Involves Personal Data? (Includes correlated anonymous Submissions if SubmissionWorker logged or PITR replayed)"}
    E -- "No (strictly intact Recital 26 aggregates/non-personal rows only)" --> F["Log in internal security register; remediate"]
    E -- Yes --> G["Start 72h Art. 33 clock ('Awareness' = reasonable certainty of breach)"]
70→    G --> H{"Affects customer Organization data (Processor role)?"}
    H -- Yes --> I["Notify affected Organization admin(s) within <= 24h (Art. 33(2))"]
    H -- No --> J["Controller-only scope (auth_user / auth_session / Site)"]
    I --> K{"Affects SurveyBeat Controller data (auth / index)?"}
    J --> K
    K -- No --> R["Customer data only. Processor notice already sent (Art. 33(2)). Do not file Art. 33(1). The customer Controller decides Art. 34. Log §6.4."]
    R --> Q
    K -- Yes --> L{"Unlikely to result in risk to rights & freedoms?"}
    L -- Yes --> M["Document non-notification rationale in Art. 33(5) register"]
    L -- No --> N["Submit Art. 33(1) notice to Supervisory Authority <= 72h (Art. 33(4) phased if ongoing)"]
80→    N --> O{"Likely to result in HIGH risk to individuals (Art. 34)?"}
    O -- Yes --> P["Notify affected individuals without undue delay (Art. 34)"]
    O -- No --> Q["Post-incident remediation, regression test & Art. 33(5) register entry"]
    P --> Q
    M --> Q
```

An `Invitation` states the `Minimum group size` and that the name is not stored with the answers, and mentions `Redaction` and AI only when `ai_processing` is on. The answer page states the `Minimum group size`, what comment `Redaction` removes (`answer.comment.disclosure`), and the AI notice when AI is on. The `person` row and membership history stay. There is no automated purge of the retained `person` row. |

The fragment is `#t=`.

The fragment claim is limited to answer links. Delivery and unsubscribe still send the token on the query string.

Comment 4641122198 addresses zero retention.

Comment 4641122204 limits the 30-day backup window to the in-app Privacy page. Invitation and answer-page copy are described as they are actually rendered.

Replies will use comment IDs so they attach correctly even if line numbers shift. I will post them via a Python script using the `gh` API. Each reply will include a markdown note block. Then I will resolve the review threads with a GraphQL query.

The GraphQL query will fetch review threads and their first comment database IDs. The resolve mutation will target only the 14 identified threads. The walkthrough summary will be left untouched.

It must not spawn subagents. It must return a verdict with file and line evidence. PR 319 will use head f7d7f391.

The 319 prompt will target the previously flagged edit-key and magic-link defects, plus the remaining legal pages. I am checking for an existing running review.

I will launch the PR 319 re-review now. I am setting up the delegate task with worktree isolation, async mode, and the antigravity provider using gemini-4-neon with high thought level. I am checking a previous delegate call format to confirm the exact syntax.

I will use the array form for the options field. I will post the GitHub replies first, then launch the reviews in parallel. The reviews are long-running, so I will not call watch_pull_request.
The corrections are on `53c767a0`. I'll reply on the fourteen threads and send the updated head back for review.

tool_input.title: Re-review PR 321
tool_input.task:
Review the current head of https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/pull/321. Head commit is 53c767a0e2d077fdd55d612540e81fc39af18ab5 on branch t3/gdpr-313-compliance-pack. Fetch that commit. Do not merge, do not enable auto-merge, do not post GitHub comments, and do not spawn subagents.

This is a documentation-only GDPR pack: docs/compliance/{ropa,dpia,breach-response-runbook,vendor-dpa-register}.md. A prior review of 3b7bb143 requested changes. Commit 53c767a0 claims to fix them. Verify each item against the source. Do not trust the commit message.

Check these claims in the new docs against the code:
1. Answer links use #t=. GET /delivery?token= and GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe?t= still send the Invitation token on the query string (issue #311). The docs must not say tokens travel only in the fragment.
2. email_send.content stores serialized StoredEmail JSON. Current Invitation/reminder rows hold an InvitationRef, not rendered HTML. Legacy WithToken rows can hold a raw token. Non-prod captured_email stores rendered html/text.
3. Browser keys are sb_edit_<roundId> and sb_answers_<roundId>, not sb_kept_*.
4. The 30-day backup window is on the in-app Privacy page (catalog.ts privacy.restore), not on every Invitation and not on the answer page. Invitation AI/redaction notice only when ai_processing is on.
5. Edit keys are generated in the browser and stored as a SHA-256 hash. INVITATION_TOKEN_KEY derives Invitation tokens only. Rotating it does not invalidate Edit keys.
6. redact() runs in the Organization Durable Object (SqlRounds.ts) after SubmissionWorker forwards raw answers. It does not run inside SubmissionWorker. The export is redact, not Redaction.redact.
7. CancelRound deletes that Round's answer, submission, and participation rows.
8. participation is (round_id, person_id). submission and answer have no person column.
9. Question text in buildThemesInput is not redacted. Comment redaction uses email local parts. PersonRecord has email and no display name, so a display name that is not in a local part is not removed.
10. OpenRouterAiClient returns AiNotConfigured only when OPENROUTER_API_KEY is missing or empty. A rotated non-empty key still sends. The runbook must say remove or empty the key.
11. pnpm test:preview-privacy without --stage, both Worker URLs, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, and CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID exits 2. Production URLs are https://dashboard.surveybeat.app and https://submit.surveybeat.app.
12. OpenRouter may retain CSAM-flagged content, including ZDR traffic (docs/research/openrouter-muse-ember.md §6). Unqualified zero prompt retention is wrong.
13. removePerson sets person.removed_at and membership.ended_at, deletes person_index, participation, and test_send, and revokes invitations. The person row stays. No automated purge.
14. Decision tree: a customer-only breach (no SurveyBeat controller data) must not dead-end. Art. 34 assessment starts at triage when high risk is already apparent.
15. BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is not a dashboard stage secret (docs/infra.md, ADR 0022). No R2 bucket is declared in infra/alchemy.run.ts. EMAIL_DEAD_LETTERED is logged in EmailDelivery.ts. The breach register is §6.4, not §7.4. Glossary: do not use User, Response, Respondent, or Responder for Person, Submission, Answer, or Team member.

Owner placeholders (legal entity name, postal address, privacy mailbox, DPIA sign-off, supervisory authority) are not defects if they stay bracketed. External vendor DPA/address claims you cannot verify from the repo stay UNVERIFIED.

Return APPROVE or REQUEST CHANGES. For each remaining defect give file, line, the doc sentence, and the source that contradicts it. Do not suggest product-code changes unless a doc sentence is still false and cannot be narrowed.

tool_input.title: Re-review PR 319
tool_input.task:
Review the current head of https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/pull/319. Head commit is f7d7f391 on branch gdpr-305-legal-pages. Fetch that commit. Confirm with git log that f7d7f391 is the head before you review. Do not merge, do not enable auto-merge, do not post GitHub comments, and do not spawn subagents.

This PR adds the public legal pages (privacy notice, terms, DPA) for GDPR issue #305. A prior review requested changes because the pages misstated the Edit key and the sign-in link lifetime.

Verify these against the code, and do not trust the commit message:
1. The first Answer sends only a hash of the Edit key (POST /first-answer, editKeyHash). Later Answers and edits send the raw Edit key (POST /answer). The server stores only the hash. apps/web/src/answer/main.ts and SubmissionRoutes.ts.
2. Sign-in codes last Policy.signIn.codeMinutes (10). Sign-in links last Policy.signIn.magicLinkMinutes (5). Sessions last Policy.signIn.sessionDays (30) and refresh on use (Better Auth updateAge).
3. Cancelling a Round deletes that Round's Answers, Submissions, and Participation records (CancelRound -> deleteSubmissionsAndParticipations). There is no automatic 24-month purge and no per-Organization retention setting. Do not accept a claim that deleting an Organization deletes remaining answers unless you find that path.
4. The AI disclosure matches buildThemesInput / AiInput: Question text is NOT redacted; each Question's dimension, score, and change are sent; comments are redacted; no Person, email, or Team name as an identifier. A name typed into Question text is sent.
5. The pages must not invent a legal entity name or postal address. privacy@surveybeat.app and German governing law are owner decisions if still flagged as unpublished or awaiting counsel.
6. Sign-in code and magic-link emails are inline strings in AuthResource.ts and do not use packages/emails Layout, so they have no legal footer. That was left on purpose. Do not treat it as an unfixed defect unless the pages claim those emails include the footer.
7. UI text comes from the message catalogs. HTML shells stay empty of visible text.

Return APPROVE or REQUEST CHANGES. For each remaining defect give file, the sentence, and the source that contradicts it. Owner decisions that are explicitly left open are not blocking.

content.text: The memory index was generated by Grok. It instructs not to edit MEMORY.md.

Neon's review of the compliance pack requested changes, and the fourteen CodeRabbit comments matched those gaps. The records now follow the code, in commit `53c767a0`.

The pre-commit gate passed: 1,441 unit tests and 244 privacy tests. The branch is pushed. Each CodeRabbit thread has a reply, and all fourteen are resolved. Nothing is merged.

What the records used to overstate, and what they say now:

- Answer links use `#t=`. Delivery and unsubscribe still send the token on the query string (issue #311).
- `email_send.content` is serialized email JSON. The browser keys are `sb_edit_` and `sb_answers_`.
- `participation` stores `person_id` and is separate from `submission`. Cancelling a Round deletes that Round's answers, submissions, and participation rows.
- Redaction runs in the Organization Durable Object and strips email local parts. `person` has no display name. Question text sent to the model is not redacted.
- Removing or emptying `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` stops AI calls. A rotated non-empty key still sends. Upstream zero-data retention does not cover OpenRouter's CSAM screening hold.
- The 30-day backup window is on the in-app Privacy page. The privacy canary check needs `--stage production` and both Worker URLs.
- A customer-only breach no longer dead-ends in the decision tree, and the individual-notification assessment starts at triage when high risk is already clear.

Two Neon re-reviews are running and will report back here: [Re-review PR 321](t3-thread://v2/461d8aa0-9e53-4578-a3c9-db2468bbeda5/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3Aa814371f-928c-4795-82bd-4ccfaa2c23fd%3Adelegate-task%3Areview-321-neon-2) and [Re-review PR 319](t3-thread://v2/461d8aa0-9e53-4578-a3c9-db2468bbeda5/thread:delegated-task:command%3Amcp%3Aa814371f-928c-4795-82bd-4ccfaa2c23fd%3Adelegate-task%3Areview-319-neon-2). No. Distributing `Invitation`s to eligible `Team` members, preventing a second `Submission` (`participation`), sending reminders only to `Team` members who have not answered, and excluding `Organization admin`s from `Team` `Result`s require knowing each `Person`'s email address and `Team` `Membership`.
2. **Are less intrusive alternatives available? Why is SurveyBeat proportionate?**  
   - **Data minimization:** Only email address, `Team` `Membership`, and time zone are needed for `Pulse` delivery. `Submission`s and `Answer`s are stored in anonymous `WITHOUT ROWID` tables with random 128-bit IDs, zero `Person` columns, zero timestamps, and zero language columns (`ropa.md` §3).
details.context_after:
- **No surveillance by management:** `Organization admin`s see zero `Result`s unless they hold a `Team` `Membership` visible to the `Team` (ADR 0003). `Minimum group size` (`>= 3`, set to `[4 or higher]`) prevents singling out individuals or subtraction attacks (ADR 0004).  
   - **Optional AI processing:** `[State whether organization.ai_processing is OFF (0) or ON (1). If ON: the payload is stored comment text, unredacted Question text, scores and changes, and redacted open Action titles, sent via OpenRouter to google-vertex/europe or amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1 with zdr: true. Upstream ZDR is not a promise that OpenRouter keeps nothing. OpenRouter may retain content it flags as potential CSAM, including ZDR traffic, and reported material is kept for one year under 18 U.S.C. § 2258A (docs/research/openrouter-muse-ember.md §6).]`

tool_input.task:
Review the current head of https://github.com/chrisdoc/surveybeat-next/pull/321. The head to approve or reject is e101a9ab on branch t3/gdpr-313-compliance-pack. Fetch it and confirm git rev-parse HEAD after checkout is e101a9ab before you review. Do not review 53c767a0 as if it were current. Do not merge, do not enable auto-merge, do not post GitHub comments, and do not spawn subagents.

Documentation only: docs/compliance/{ropa,dpia,breach-response-runbook,vendor-dpa-register}.md.

Commit e101a9ab qualifies four follow-ups. Verify each against source, and do not trust the commit message:
1. QuestionText in packages/domain/src/pulses/Question.ts is a trimmed string of 1 to 200 characters. It does not reject emails or names. buildThemesInput sends q.text unredacted. The docs must say the AI payload has no dedicated identity fields, and that an email or name typed into a Question is still sent. R-05 residual is Medium for that reason.
2. redact in packages/domain/src/privacy/Redaction.ts skips candidates whose normalized length is under 2. A one-character email local part can remain as a word. A full email address is still replaced by the email pattern. The docs must not say every local part is removed.
3. directory.removePerson sets person.removed_at and membership.ended_at. It does not delete the person row. There is no erasure command for that row. The docs must say that erasure is not available yet.
4. Also re-check the earlier corrections still hold: answer links use #t=; GET /delivery?token= and GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe?t= still send the token (issue #311); email_send.content is StoredEmail JSON; browser keys are sb_edit_ and sb_answers_; participation has person_id; CancelRound deletes that Round's answers, submissions, and participation rows; redaction runs in the Organization Durable Object; OpenRouterAiClient fails closed only when the key is missing or empty; the canary sweep needs --stage, both Worker URLs, and the two Cloudflare env vars; OpenRouter CSAM retention is disclosed; BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is not a dashboard secret; no R2 bucket is declared.

Return APPROVE or REQUEST CHANGES. For each remaining defect give file, the sentence, and the source that contradicts it. codecov/project is not a required check and a docs-only coverage comparison against an older base is not a defect.

`codecov/project` failed on a docs-only change, and four CodeRabbit follow-ups were real. Those four are fixed in `e101a9ab`. The other threads were the earlier findings, already corrected and resolved.

**Verdict: REQUEST CHANGES.** Two statements in the notice are false against the live code. The issue's done-when says every disclosure must be "accurate against the live codebase". Both fixes are wording changes in the catalog. Everything else holds up.

I checked out head `e113ad04` in a throwaway worktree, then removed it. The web build, `budget.test.ts`, the site, message, Legal and email tests (105 passed), `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint` and `format:check` all pass.

## Blocking

1. **The notice says the Edit key never leaves the browser except as a hash. It does.**
   - `apps/web/src/messages/legalPrivacy.ts`, `legal.privacy.s09.tedit.what`: "It never leaves the browser except as a hash."
   - In the code, `apps/web/src/answer/main.ts:641-645` sends the raw `editKey` to `POST /answer` on every later save. `SubmissionRoutes.ts:280-284` hashes it on the server.
   - ADR 0005 says so too: "sends only its SHA-256 hash with the first Answer. Later Answers and changes carry only the Edit key."
   - Suggested wording: only a hash goes with the first answer; to change answers the browser sends the key itself over HTTPS; the server stores only the hash.

2. **The retention text describes a setting and a deletion that don't exist.**
   - `legalPrivacy.ts`, `s03.tanswers.retention`: "24 months unless the Organization sets another period."
   - `legalAgreements.ts`, `legal.dpa.s08.p1`: Submissions "are deleted when the Organization's retention period for them ends."
   - Nothing in the migrations or code stores a retention period or deletes anything on one. SPEC §5.3 calls for the setting, but it isn't built.
   - Stating 24 months as policy is fine; the issue asks for it. Saying it is configurable and enforced claims a retention job that doesn't exist. The PR body admits this, but the pages don't.

## Minor inaccuracies

- **Sign-in link lifetime is wrong.** `s03.tsignin.retention` and `s03.temail.retention` say codes and links last `{codeMinutes}` (10) minutes. `Policy.signIn.magicLinkMinutes` is 5.
- **Viewers are missing.** `legal.dpa.s02.p1` lists data subjects as "members, Leads and admins". The glossary's Membership roles also include viewer.
- **"Every request is checked against the session" is too broad.** `legal.dpa.s05.li6` says this, but the answer and submit requests authenticate with an Invitation token or Edit key, not a session.
- **One unprotected case from ADR 0005 is left out.** `legal.privacy.s04.p3` lists restores and edge logs. ADR 0005 also names an operator changing the code to start logging.
- **The answer page has almost no room left.** It is 8126 of 8192 bytes, so the next string added there will break the budget.

## Confirmed

- **Pages:** all four prerender into `dist-site` with zero `<script` tags. `htmlHandling: "auto-trailing-slash"` serves `/privacy` from `privacy.html`. `site.html` still has an empty `<title>` and no visible text, and no new shell was added.
- **Art. 13/14 items:**
  - the controller/processor split;
  - data categories with their Art. 6 bases;
  - anonymous Submissions store no Person and no time, are non-personal under Recital 26, and survive deletion;
  - the 30-day restore window;
  - the session cookie, which matches `AuthHandlers.ts:30-34`;
  - the `sb_edit_`, `sb_answers_` and `sb_token` storage keys, with the 1-year lifetime matching `kept-answers.ts`;
  - Art. 15–22 rights with a 30-day response;
  - SCCs and the Data Privacy Framework;
  - EU-only zero-retention AI routing, which matches the request shape in `OpenRouterAiClient.ts` and ADR 0015.
- **Sub-processors:** Cloudflare, OpenRouter, `google-vertex/europe` and `amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1` are each listed with purpose, region and transfer basis. That meets ADR 0015.
- **Other claims checked against code:**
  - The Durable Object and D1 location is correctly described as not pinned; there is no `jurisdiction` setting in the code.
  - Pulses are anonymous only (`CHECK (anonymity_mode IN ('anonymous'))`), and the notice correctly offers no confidential mode.
  - Removing a Person deletes their Participation records.
  - Organization admins have no `team.viewResults` permission.
  - The answer page and Invitation do show the AI notice.
  - The redaction list matches ADR 0009.
- **Links:**
  - The landing page uses the shared `siteFooter`.
  - Every app view, including sign-in (`session.ts:119`) and the signed-in shell (`directory.ts:297`), goes through `pageShell`, so all of them get the footer.
  - The in-app `/privacy` screen has its own links block.
  - The answer page has a footer, and the email layout has links in both the HTML and text parts.
  - Staging intentionally links to the production `https://surveybeat.app`.
- **Answer page:** the budget test passes on the new markup. The minified bootstrap passes `node --check`. Every statement in it ends in `;` or `}`, there are no `//` comments, and the token regex is intact. The body whitespace stripping only touches gaps between block elements, and no answer code walks text nodes.
- **German law and the liability clause** appear only as chosen wording in the Terms. No ADR or SPEC section decides them.
- **Boundaries:** `Legal.ts` imports nothing. The answer entry's imports are unchanged; only `vite.config.ts` imports the domain package. No D1 writes were added, and no privacy invariant is weakened.

## Owner decisions, not code defects

- **No legal entity or postal address.** The pages don't make up details, but they also don't say anything is missing: they just say "SurveyBeat runs surveybeat.app". Art. 13(1)(a) needs the controller's identity and address. The issue also asks for DPO contact details, and the pages don't address that either.
- **The Terms have no acceptance step.** They say an admin who creates an Organization "accepts the terms", but the product has no click-through.
- **Some promises have no mechanism behind them yet:** emailing admins before a sub-processor change or a notice change, and suspension notices.
- **"Stays in the EU, so no transfer"** for Google Cloud and AWS is a legal position, given that both parent companies are in the US.
- The governing-law and liability wording, the `privacy@surveybeat.app` mailbox, and the hard-coded effective date of 20 November 2026.

## Unverified

- **Where OpenRouter itself handles comment text.** The client calls the global `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions` (`OpenRouterAiClient.ts:16`), and code alone doesn't pin where OpenRouter's proxy runs. "The service runs in the EU" matches ADR 0015's own claim, but I couldn't confirm it.
- Whether Cloudflare's and OpenRouter's data processing terms really contain SCCs, and whether each is DPF-certified.
- Whether removing a Person ever purges the `person` row. Removal sets `removedAt`, and I found no purge path behind "deleted on request".
- How long Cloudflare keeps Workers Logs.
- The Lighthouse gate on the new answer-page footer. I didn't run it.

content.text:
The Opus review of PR 319 evaluated a stale head commit.

Neon re-review of f7d7f391 confirmed the two blocking fixes. Three remaining issues were found in PR 319:

- AI disclosure in legalPrivacy.ts omits a name, Person, Team, Round, or time, but the question text is unredacted.
- The same disclosure issue appears in legalAgreements.ts for the Google sub-processor purpose.
- The privacy edit key body in catalog.ts understates that every answer after the first sends the raw key.

Three minor issues may still be open:

- Viewers might be missing from legal.dpa.s02.p1.
- The phrase "every request is checked against the session" remains in legalAgreements.ts line 89.
- ADR 0005 may omit operator code changes to start logging from privacy.s04.p3.

A privacy disclosure in legalPrivacy.ts incorrectly states that removing a Person deletes their data on request. The removePerson function does not delete the person row and no erasure command exists. This is a real defect that needs correction. A minor double space before "Until it is" was also spotted.

I will read the relevant strings and tests before updating them. The fix spans catalog, legalPrivacy, legalAgreements, and tests. I will not add strings to the answer page.

I will fix the PR 319 wording myself because the exact sentences are fully specified.

For PR 321 neon-2, two items remain on 53c767a0. The unsubscribe endpoint may still say GET instead of POST. LIA line 69 still omits an unqualified Recital 26 reference. The review-321-neon-3 task is in flight on e101a9ab.

Opus reviewed an old legal-pages commit. Neon reviewed the current one and still wants three wording fixes. The compliance pack has two leftover false sentences. I'll confirm those against the code and correct them.

content.text:
70→    "The data subjects are the Organization's People: members, Leads and admins. The data is their email address, role, Team Membership, time zone and language, Invitation and reminder settings and delivery records, Participation records, and the comment text they enter. Anonymous Submissions hold no Person and no time and are not personal data. We do not process special categories of data on purpose. Comments are free text, and the Organization should tell People not to put such data in them.",
  "legal.dpa.s03.title": "Instructions",
  "legal.dpa.s03.p1":
    "SurveyBeat processes personal data only on the Organization's documented instructions, which are these terms and the settings the Organization chooses in the product. If the law requires other processing, SurveyBeat tells the Organization first unless the law forbids it. SurveyBeat tells the Organization at once if it believes an instruction breaks data protection law.",
  "legal.dpa.s04.title": "Confidentiality",
  "legal.dpa.s04.p1":
    "Everyone at SurveyBeat who can reach personal data is bound to confidentiality and gets access only as far as the work needs.",
  "legal.dpa.s05.title": "Security measures (Article 32)",
  "legal.dpa.s05.p1": "SurveyBeat keeps at least these technical and organizational measures:",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li1":
80→    "each Organization's data sits in its own Durable Object, with no records shared between Organizations",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li2":
    "an anonymous Submission holds no Person and no time, and its table has no Person column. Participation records are stored apart from answers",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li3":
    "Invitation tokens travel in the part of the link after the hash, so the answer page request never sends one. They are stored only as hashes. The first Answer sends only a hash of the Edit key. Later Answers and edits send the Edit key over HTTPS, and the server stores only that hash",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li4":
    "the Worker that receives anonymous answers keeps no logs, traces or analytics, and a test checks it",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li5":
    "comments are redacted when stored, and nothing is shown below the minimum group size, including by subtraction between groups",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li6": "every request is checked against the session, with access rules defined in one place",
90→  "legal.dpa.s05.li7":
    "traffic is encrypted in transit and storage is encrypted at rest. Only named operators can start a restore, and backups are kept for {restoreDays} days",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li8": "privacy tests that prove these properties must pass before a change is released",
  "legal.dpa.s06.title": "Sub-processors",
  "legal.dpa.s06.p1":
    "The Organization gives SurveyBeat general authorization to use the processors on the Sub-processors page. SurveyBeat imposes on each of them the same data protection duties as this agreement and stays responsible to the Organization for them.",
  "legal.dpa.s06.p2":
    "SurveyBeat tells the Organization's admins by email before it adds or replaces a sub-processor, early enough for the Organization to object. If the Organization objects on reasonable grounds and the parties cannot agree, the Organization may end the agreement.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.title": "Help, breaches and audits",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p1":
100→    "SurveyBeat helps the Organization answer requests from data subjects, and meet its duties under Articles 32 to 36, as far as the nature of the processing allows. If a request reaches SurveyBeat directly, it passes it to the Organization.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p2":
    "SurveyBeat tells the Organization's admins without undue delay after it becomes aware of a personal data breach, and gives what it knows about the nature of the breach, the data and people concerned, the likely consequences and the steps taken.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p3":
    "SurveyBeat gives the Organization the information needed to show compliance with this agreement, and allows audits by the Organization or an auditor it names, with reasonable notice, normally once a year and again after a breach. The audit may not disclose other Organizations' data.",
  "legal.dpa.s08.title": "Return and deletion",
  "legal.dpa.s08.p1":
    "When the services end, SurveyBeat returns the Organization's personal data on request in a common machine-readable format and then deletes it, unless the law requires it to keep a copy. Copies in backups are overwritten as the {restoreDays}-day restore window passes. Anonymous Submissions are not personal data. Automatic deletion at the end of the retention period is not in place yet. Cancelling a Round deletes that Round's Answers, Submissions and Participation records.",
  "legal.dpa.s09.title": "Transfers",
  "legal.dpa.s09.p1":
110→    "A transfer of personal data outside the EU and EEA takes place only under an adequacy decision, the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or another safeguard Chapter V of the GDPR allows. Comment text for AI processing goes only to endpoints in the EU.",
  "legal.dpa.s10.title": "Liability and order of terms",
  "legal.dpa.s10.p1":
    "Liability follows the Terms of Service. Where this agreement and the Terms disagree about personal data, this agreement applies.",

  "legal.subprocessors.title": "Sub-processors",
  "legal.subprocessors.description":
    "The companies that process personal data for SurveyBeat's customers, with the purpose, location and transfer basis of each.",
  "legal.subprocessors.lede":
    "These are the sub-processors that SurveyBeat uses under the Data Processing Agreement. We tell Organization admins by email before we add or replace one. Effective {effective}.",
120→  "legal.subprocessors.s01.title": "Current sub-processors",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.th.name": "Sub-processor",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.th.purpose": "What it does for SurveyBeat",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.th.location": "Where",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.th.basis": "Transfer basis",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tcloudflare.name": "Cloudflare, Inc.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tcloudflare.purpose":
    "Hosts everything: Workers, Durable Objects (each Organization's data), D1 (the sign-in and lookup index), Queues, static pages, and Email Sending for Invitations and sign-in codes.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tcloudflare.location":
    "Cloudflare's global network. Where Durable Object and D1 data is stored is chosen by Cloudflare, and SurveyBeat sets no jurisdiction limit today.",
130→  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tcloudflare.basis":
    "Standard Contractual Clauses in Cloudflare's data processing terms, and the EU–US Data Privacy Framework.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.topenrouter.name": "OpenRouter, Inc.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.topenrouter.purpose":
    "Routes AI requests for comment themes and discussion guides. Used only when an Organization admin turns AI processing on. Requests demand zero data retention, and prompt and output logging is off.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.topenrouter.location":
    "The United States for its account and abuse-monitoring data. It sends comment text only to the two EU endpoints below.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.topenrouter.basis":
    "Standard Contractual Clauses in OpenRouter's data processing terms for its own data. Comment text goes to the EU only.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tgoogle.name": "Google Cloud (google-vertex/europe)",
140→  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tgoogle.purpose":
    "Runs the AI model for comment themes and discussion guides on a zero-retention endpoint. A request can include Question text, each Question's dimension, Question and Dimension scores and changes, whether a change is larger than usual, redacted comment text tied to a Question position, and redacted titles of open Actions. It does not include a name, a Person, a Team, a Round or a time.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tgoogle.location": "European Union",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tgoogle.basis": "Stays in the EU, so no transfer.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.taws.name": "Amazon Web Services (amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1)",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.taws.purpose":
    "The second EU zero-retention endpoint for the same request. Used only when the first cannot serve it.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.taws.location": "Ireland, European Union",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.taws.basis": "Stays in the EU, so no transfer.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s02.title": "How AI processing is limited",

content.text:
480→  "privacy.anonymity.body":
    "Anonymous Submissions store no name and no time. Your name, email, and IP address are never recorded with your answers, and answers are saved without a timestamp so they cannot be linked to access logs.",
  "privacy.comments.title": "Comment redaction",
  "privacy.comments.body":
    "Comments are redacted before storage. Names of people in your Organization, email addresses, phone numbers, handles, and URLs are automatically stripped. Other phrasing is kept intact, so please leave out personal details.",
  "privacy.restore.title": "{days}-day point-in-time restore window",
  "privacy.restore.body":
    "Database backups are kept for up to {days} days point-in-time strictly for disaster recovery. Backups are encrypted at rest and purged permanently after {days} days.",
  "privacy.editKey.title": "Changing your answers",
  "privacy.editKey.body":
490→    "The Edit key stays in this browser. The first Answer sends only its hash. Later changes send the key over HTTPS, and SurveyBeat stores only the hash. Losing or clearing the Edit key means answers cannot be changed.",
  "privacy.restoreTrigger.title": "Who can trigger a restore",
  "privacy.restoreTrigger.body":
    "Only authorized infrastructure operators with verified credentials can initiate a disaster recovery restore. Organization admins and Leads cannot inspect raw backups or trigger restores.",
  "history.title": "My history",
  "history.intro":
    "The check-ins you took part in. Your own answers are kept only in this browser, for one year. SurveyBeat never stores which answers are yours.",
  "history.empty": "You haven't taken part in a check-in yet.",
  "history.noAnswersHere":
    "Your answers aren't on this device. They stay only in the browser you answered in, and SurveyBeat can't restore them. The Team's scores are still shown.",

1→# SurveyBeat orchestration

Model roles for implementing and reviewing surveybeat-next issues.

## Routing

- Workers are Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 4 Hydrogen; the reviewer is Opus 5.5.
- Workers implement in isolated worktrees and open PRs; Opus reviews before merge.
- Do not auto-merge.
10→- Open GDPR and Release 3 issues go through that orchestration.
- When Opus is unavailable, send delegated work, including PR review, to Neon instead of waiting for the Opus rate limit to lift.
- Gemini 4 Neon is available as antigravity model gemini-4-neon (option thought_level) and as opencode model opencode/gemini-4-neon (option variant).

50→## 3. Why Anonymous `submission` and `answer` Rows Are Non-Personal Data (GDPR Recital 26)

Under GDPR Article 4(1) and Recital 26, data is outside the scope of personal data protection if it is rendered anonymous in such a manner that the data subject is not or is no longer identifiable, taking account of **"all the means reasonably likely to be used, such as singling out, either by the controller or by another person to identify the natural person directly or indirectly."**

The `submission` and `answer` tables (`packages/cloudflare/migrations/0008_submissions.sql`) are built so a stored row has no column that identifies a `Person`. That structural split is test-verified (`Submissions.privacy.test.ts`, `Unlinkability.privacy.test.ts`). It is not a claim that every stored comment is non-personal data. A comment can still identify its author through a unique anecdote that rule-based `Redaction` does not remove. Where that happens, treat the comment as personal data for retention and for rights requests. The controls below are what the schema and the ingestion path actually do:

1. **Structural decoupling in schema (`0008_submissions.sql`, `0007_invitations.sql`):**
   - `submission` contains only `(id, round_id, edit_key_hash)` and `answer` contains only `(submission_id, question_version_id, value, comment)`.
   - `participation` contains only `(round_id, person_id)`.
   - Neither `submission`, `answer`, nor `participation` has any timestamp column—going stricter than SPEC §5.3's coarse day bucket (ADR 0005).
60→   - No `submission`, `answer`, or `participation` table stores a `locale` or language column, preventing language-based singling out in small `Team`s (`Submissions.privacy.test.ts` A10).
   - All three tables are declared `WITHOUT ROWID`, and `submission.id` is a random 128-bit hex key (`secureRandomBytes` in `SqlRounds.ts`), eliminating SQLite insertion-order `rowid` correlation (`Submissions.privacy.test.ts` A1, A2).
2. **Zero-observability ingestion boundary (`SubmissionWorker.ts`, `SubmissionRoutes.ts`, ADR 0005):**
   - Answer links put the `Invitation` token in the URL fragment (`#t=`), so opening the answer page does not send it. `GET /delivery?token=` and `GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe?t=` on `MainWorker` still send that token in the query string, where Workers Logs and `Referer` can see it (issue #311).
   - `SubmissionWorker` accepts credentials only in the POST JSON body and rejects any request carrying both an `Invitation` token and an `Edit key` (`SubmissionRoutes.privacy.test.ts` A5).
   - `SubmissionWorker` has `observability.enabled: false`, `logs.enabled: false`, `traces.enabled: false`, `logpush: false`, `tailConsumers: []`, and `streamingTailConsumers: []`, verified on every stage by `pnpm check:observability` (`infra/scripts/check-observability.ts`) and `pnpm test:preview-privacy` (`infra/tests/privacy/canary-sweep.ts`).
   - `SubmissionWorker` never returns stored `Answer`s for an `Edit key` (`SubmissionRoutes.privacy.test.ts`).
3. **Store-time `Redaction` (ADR 0009, `packages/domain/src/privacy/Redaction.ts`):**
   - Before any `Answer` comment is written to SQLite, `recordFirstAnswer` and `saveAnswer` (`SqlRounds.ts`) call `redact` (`Redaction.ts`) inside the `Organization` Durable Object. `SubmissionWorker` forwards the raw answers over Durable Object RPC and does not redact them. The roster is the directory's `PersonRecord` list: email, and no display name. `redact` strips email local parts (split on `.`, `_`, and `-`), email addresses, phone numbers, `@handles`, and URLs, replacing them with `[name]`, `[email]`, `[phone]`, `[handle]`, and `[link]`. A candidate shorter than 2 characters is skipped, so a one-character local part can remain when it appears as a word. A full email address is still replaced. A display name that is not part of an email local part is not removed.
   - Raw comment text exists solely in transient request memory and is never persisted or logged (`Submissions.privacy.test.ts` A4b).
70→4. **Statistical unlinkability & disclosure controls (`Unlinkability.privacy.test.ts`, `Results.privacy.test.ts`, `Themes.privacy.test.ts`):**
   - `Unlinkability.privacy.test.ts` and `Submissions.privacy.test.ts` (A4) prove that dumping `participation` and `submission` in key order yields no better than random-guess linkage across `rank`, `keyOrder`, `rowid`, and `sharedColumns` attacks.
   - `Minimum group size` (`>= 3`, default `4`, ADR 0004) blocks any `Result`, `Question` score, `Dimension` score, or subtraction-derived sub-group below `N`; no live `Result`s are shown while a `Round` is `Open`; `Lead` comments are unlinked from ratings and `Submission` order; `Comment theme`s require `>= 2` supporting comments and pass a 6-word anti-quote filter (ADR 0016, ADR 0019).
5. **Survival upon erasure (`Submissions.privacy.test.ts` A9):**
   - `directory.removePerson` sets `person.removed_at` and `membership.ended_at`. It deletes that `Person`'s `participation` rows, revokes `invitation`s, deletes `test_send`s, and deletes `person_index` in D1. The `person` row and membership history stay. There is no automated purge of that row, and no command that erases it or the membership history. That erasure is not available yet. `submission` and `answer` rows also stay. They are free of a `Person` column. A comment that still identifies its author remains personal data, so erasure of that comment is not done by `removePerson`.

### Residual Caveats Documented for Transparency

- **Free-text self-identification:** `redact` strips email local parts from the roster, emails, phones, handles, and URLs. It does not strip a display name that is absent from those local parts, a nickname, or a unique anecdote. The answer page says what is and is not removed (`apps/web/src/messages/answer.ts` `answer.comment.disclosure`). The in-app Privacy page has a separate `privacy.comments.body` in `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts`.
- **30-day Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) window (ADR 0005):** Replaying the Durable Object write-ahead log (WAL) during a PITR restore could correlate writes made in the same transaction. SurveyBeat mitigates this through strict operator-only access controls, a hard 30-day backup expiry (`Policy.backupRetentionDays = 30`), and explicit user-facing disclosure (`catalog.ts` `privacy.restore`, `privacy.restoreTrigger`).

60→   - **Data minimization:** Only email address, `Team` `Membership`, and time zone are needed for `Pulse` delivery. `Submission`s and `Answer`s are stored in anonymous `WITHOUT ROWID` tables with random 128-bit IDs, zero `Person` columns, zero timestamps, and zero language columns (`ropa.md` §3).  
   - **Store-time `Redaction`:** Before a comment is stored, `redact` removes email addresses, phone numbers, `@handles`, URLs, and roster email local parts of at least 2 characters. A shorter local part can remain when it appears as a word. `person` stores email and no display name, so a name that is not in an email local part is not removed (`Redaction.ts`, `ropa.md` §4). `Question` text sent to the model is not redacted and may contain a name or an email address. `QuestionText` does not reject that.  
   - **No surveillance by management:** `Organization admin`s see zero `Result`s unless they hold a `Team` `Membership` visible to the `Team` (ADR 0003). `Minimum group size` (`>= 3`, set to `[4 or higher]`) prevents singling out individuals or subtraction attacks (ADR 0004).  
   - **Optional AI processing:** `[State whether organization.ai_processing is OFF (0) or ON (1). If ON: the payload is stored comment text, unredacted Question text, scores and changes, and redacted open Action titles, sent via OpenRouter to google-vertex/europe or amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1 with zdr: true. Upstream ZDR is not a promise that OpenRouter keeps nothing. OpenRouter may retain content it flags as potential CSAM, including ZDR traffic, and reported material is kept for one year under 18 U.S.C. § 2258A (docs/research/openrouter-muse-ember.md §6).]`

#### Part 3: Balancing Test — Do the data subjects' interests or rights override the legitimate interest?

| Factor | Assessment for `[Organization Name]` |
| --- | --- |
| **Nature of data** | Directory & delivery metadata (work email, `Team` `Membership`, `Round` `Participation record` without timestamp). Stored `Answer`s/comments are anonymous under Recital 26 (`ropa.md` §3). Special-category data (Art. 9) is not solicited. |
70→| **Power imbalance (workplace context)** | Because `[Organization Name]` is the employer, `Team` members could fear retaliation if answers were attributable. SurveyBeat neutralizes this structurally: `Submission`s cannot be joined to `Person`s, `Minimum group size` blocks small-group exposure, `Lead`s see no live `Result`s while a `Round` is `Open`, and `Organization admin`s see no `Result`s. |
| **Reasonable expectations of `Team` members** | Periodic anonymous team feedback check-ins are standard in modern workplaces. An `Invitation` states the `Minimum group size` and that the name is not stored with the answers, and mentions `Redaction` and AI only when `ai_processing` is on. The answer page states the `Minimum group size`, what comment `Redaction` removes (`answer.comment.disclosure`), and the AI notice when AI is on. The 30-day backup window is on the in-app Privacy page only (`catalog.ts` `privacy.restore`). |
| **Autonomy & Right to Object (Art. 21)** | Participation in `Pulse`s is voluntary. `Team` members can opt out of reminders per `Pulse` (`GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe`, RFC 8058) or object to directory or reminder processing by contacting `[Internal HR / Privacy Contact]`. `directory.removePerson` sets `person.removed_at` and `membership.ended_at`, deletes `person_index`, `participation`, and `test_send`, and revokes `Invitation`s. The `person` row and membership history stay. There is no automated purge of the retained `person` row, and no command that erases that row or the membership history. That erasure is not available yet. |
| **Safeguards** | Zero-observability `SubmissionWorker`, encrypted storage, EU-pinned ZDR AI (if enabled), and documented internal policy prohibiting attempts to coerce or guess who wrote specific comments. |

#### Part 4: Outcome & Sign-Off

- **Assessment Conclusion:** `[Legitimate Interest (Art. 6(1)(f)) IS / IS NOT valid for this rollout, subject to the safeguards listed above and informing Team members via our internal employee privacy notice.]`
- **Conditions / Controls Required Before Launch:**
  1. Set `Minimum group size` to `[>= 4]`.
