content.text:
60→  "legal.dpa.title": "Data Processing Agreement",
  "legal.dpa.description":
    "The Article 28 agreement between an Organization and SurveyBeat: instructions, security measures, sub-processors, breach notice and return or deletion of data.",
  "legal.dpa.lede":
    "This agreement applies between an Organization, the controller, and SurveyBeat, the processor, whenever SurveyBeat processes personal data for the Organization. The legal name and postal address of the operator are not published on this page yet. It is part of the Terms of Service and meets GDPR Article 28(3). Effective {effective}.",
  "legal.dpa.s01.title": "Subject matter, duration and nature",
  "legal.dpa.s01.p1":
    "SurveyBeat processes personal data to run Pulses for the Organization: storing People and Teams, sending Invitations and reminders by email, collecting Submissions, working out Results and, if an admin turns it on, writing comment themes and discussion guides. The processing lasts as long as the Organization uses SurveyBeat and ends as clause 8 says.",
  "legal.dpa.s02.title": "Data and people concerned",
  "legal.dpa.s02.p1":
70→    "The data subjects are the Organization's People: members, Leads and admins. The data is their email address, role, Team Membership, time zone and language, Invitation and reminder settings and delivery records, Participation records, and the comment text they enter. Anonymous Submissions hold no Person and no time and are not personal data. We do not process special categories of data on purpose. Comments are free text, and the Organization should tell People not to put such data in them.",
  "legal.dpa.s03.title": "Instructions",
  "legal.dpa.s03.p1":
    "SurveyBeat processes personal data only on the Organization's documented instructions, which are these terms and the settings the Organization chooses in the product. If the law requires other processing, SurveyBeat tells the Organization first unless the law forbids it. SurveyBeat tells the Organization at once if it believes an instruction breaks data protection law.",
  "legal.dpa.s04.title": "Confidentiality",
  "legal.dpa.s04.p1":
    "Everyone at SurveyBeat who can reach personal data is bound to confidentiality and gets access only as far as the work needs.",
  "legal.dpa.s05.title": "Security measures (Article 32)",
  "legal.dpa.s05.p1": "SurveyBeat keeps at least these technical and organizational measures:",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li1":
80→    "each Organization's data sits in its own Durable Object, with no records shared between Organizations",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li2":
    "an anonymous Submission holds no Person and no time, and its table has no Person column. Participation records are stored apart from answers",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li3":
    "Invitation tokens travel in the part of the link after the hash, so the answer page request never sends one. They are stored only as hashes. The first Answer sends only a hash of the Edit key. Later Answers and edits send the Edit key over HTTPS, and the server stores only that hash",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li4":
    "the Worker that receives anonymous answers keeps no logs, traces or analytics, and a test checks it",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li5":
    "comments are redacted when stored, and nothing is shown below the minimum group size, including by subtraction between groups",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li6": "every request is checked against the session, with access rules defined in one place",
90→  "legal.dpa.s05.li7":
    "traffic is encrypted in transit and storage is encrypted at rest. Only named operators can start a restore, and backups are kept for {restoreDays} days",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li8": "privacy tests that prove these properties must pass before a change is released",
  "legal.dpa.s06.title": "Sub-processors",
  "legal.dpa.s06.p1":
    "The Organization gives SurveyBeat general authorization to use the processors on the Sub-processors page. SurveyBeat imposes on each of them the same data protection duties as this agreement and stays responsible to the Organization for them.",
  "legal.dpa.s06.p2":
    "SurveyBeat tells the Organization's admins by email before it adds or replaces a sub-processor, early enough for the Organization to object. If the Organization objects on reasonable grounds and the parties cannot agree, the Organization may end the agreement.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.title": "Help, breaches and audits",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p1":
100→    "SurveyBeat helps the Organization answer requests from data subjects, and meet its duties under Articles 32 to 36, as far as the nature of the processing allows. If a request reaches SurveyBeat directly, it passes it to the Organization.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p2":
    "SurveyBeat tells the Organization's admins without undue delay after it becomes aware of a personal data breach, and gives what it knows about the nature of the breach, the data and people concerned, the likely consequences and the steps taken.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p3":
    "SurveyBeat gives the Organization the information needed to show compliance with this agreement, and allows audits by the Organization or an auditor it names, with reasonable notice, normally once a year and again after a breach. The audit may not disclose other Organizations' data.",
  "legal.dpa.s08.title": "Return and deletion",
  "legal.dpa.s08.p1":
    "When the services end, SurveyBeat returns the Organization's personal data on request in a common machine-readable format and then deletes it, unless the law requires it to keep a copy. Copies in backups are overwritten as the {restoreDays}-day restore window passes. Anonymous Submissions are not personal data. Automatic deletion at the end of the retention period is not in place yet. Cancelling a Round deletes that Round's Answers, Submissions and Participation records.",
  "legal.dpa.s09.title": "Transfers",
  "legal.dpa.s09.p1":
110→    "A transfer of personal data outside the EU and EEA takes place only under an adequacy decision, the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or another safeguard Chapter V of the GDPR allows. Comment text for AI processing goes only to endpoints in the EU.",
  "legal.dpa.s10.title": "Liability and order of terms",
  "legal.dpa.s10.p1":
    "Liability follows the Terms of Service. Where this agreement and the Terms disagree about personal data, this agreement applies.",

  "legal.subprocessors.title": "Sub-processors",
  "legal.subprocessors.description":
    "The companies that process personal data for SurveyBeat's customers, with the purpose, location and transfer basis of each.",
  "legal.subprocessors.lede":
    "These are the sub-processors that SurveyBeat uses under the Data Processing Agreement. We tell Organization admins by email before we add or replace one. Effective {effective}.",
120→  "legal.subprocessors.s01.title": "Current sub-processors",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.th.name": "Sub-processor",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.th.purpose": "What it does for SurveyBeat",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.th.location": "Where",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.th.basis": "Transfer basis",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tcloudflare.name": "Cloudflare, Inc.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tcloudflare.purpose":
    "Hosts everything: Workers, Durable Objects (each Organization's data), D1 (the sign-in and lookup index), Queues, static pages, and Email Sending for Invitations and sign-in codes.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tcloudflare.location":
    "Cloudflare's global network. Where Durable Object and D1 data is stored is chosen by Cloudflare, and SurveyBeat sets no jurisdiction limit today.",
130→  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tcloudflare.basis":
    "Standard Contractual Clauses in Cloudflare's data processing terms, and the EU–US Data Privacy Framework.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.topenrouter.name": "OpenRouter, Inc.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.topenrouter.purpose":
    "Routes AI requests for comment themes and discussion guides. Used only when an Organization admin turns AI processing on. Requests demand zero data retention, and prompt and output logging is off.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.topenrouter.location":
    "The United States for its account and abuse-monitoring data. It sends comment text only to the two EU endpoints below.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.topenrouter.basis":
    "Standard Contractual Clauses in OpenRouter's data processing terms for its own data. Comment text goes to the EU only.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tgoogle.name": "Google Cloud (google-vertex/europe)",
140→  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tgoogle.purpose":
    "Runs the AI model for comment themes and discussion guides on a zero-retention endpoint. A request can include Question text, each Question's dimension, Question and Dimension scores and changes, whether a change is larger than usual, redacted comment text tied to a Question position, and redacted titles of open Actions. It does not include a name, a Person, a Team, a Round or a time.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tgoogle.location": "European Union",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.tgoogle.basis": "Stays in the EU, so no transfer.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.taws.name": "Amazon Web Services (amazon-bedrock/eu-west-1)",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.taws.purpose":
    "The second EU zero-retention endpoint for the same request. Used only when the first cannot serve it.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.taws.location": "Ireland, European Union",
  "legal.subprocessors.s01.taws.basis": "Stays in the EU, so no transfer.",
  "legal.subprocessors.s02.title": "How AI processing is limited",

60→  "legal.dpa.title": "Data Processing Agreement",
  "legal.dpa.description":
    "The Article 28 agreement between an Organization and SurveyBeat: instructions, security measures, sub-processors, breach notice and return or deletion of data.",
  "legal.dpa.lede":
    "This agreement applies between an Organization, the controller, and SurveyBeat, the processor, whenever SurveyBeat processes personal data for the Organization. The legal name and postal address of the operator are not published on this page yet. It is part of the Terms of Service and meets GDPR Article 28(3). Effective {effective}.",
  "legal.dpa.s01.title": "Subject matter, duration and nature",
  "legal.dpa.s01.p1":
    "SurveyBeat processes personal data to run Pulses for the Organization: storing People and Teams, sending Invitations and reminders by email, collecting Submissions, working out Results and, if an admin turns it on, writing comment themes and discussion guides. The processing lasts as long as the Organization uses SurveyBeat and ends as clause 8 says.",
  "legal.dpa.s02.title": "Data and people concerned",
  "legal.dpa.s02.p1":
70→    "The data subjects are the Organization's People: members, Leads and admins. The data is their email address, role, Team Membership, time zone and language, Invitation and reminder settings and delivery records, Participation records, and the comment text they enter. Anonymous Submissions hold no Person and no time and are not personal data. We do not process special categories of data on purpose. Comments are free text, and the Organization should tell People not to put such data in them.",
  "legal.dpa.s03.title": "Instructions",
  "legal.dpa.s03.p1":
    "SurveyBeat processes personal data only on the Organization's documented instructions, which are these terms and the settings the Organization chooses in the product. If the law requires other processing, SurveyBeat tells the Organization first unless the law forbids it. SurveyBeat tells the Organization at once if it believes an instruction breaks data protection law.",
  "legal.dpa.s04.title": "Confidentiality",
  "legal.dpa.s04.p1":
    "Everyone at SurveyBeat who can reach personal data is bound to confidentiality and gets access only as far as the work needs.",
  "legal.dpa.s05.title": "Security measures (Article 32)",
  "legal.dpa.s05.p1": "SurveyBeat keeps at least these technical and organizational measures:",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li1":
80→    "each Organization's data sits in its own Durable Object, with no records shared between Organizations",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li2":
    "an anonymous Submission holds no Person and no time, and its table has no Person column. Participation records are stored apart from answers",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li3":
    "Invitation tokens travel in the part of the link after the hash, so the answer page request never sends one. They are stored only as hashes. The first Answer sends only a hash of the Edit key. Later Answers and edits send the Edit key over HTTPS, and the server stores only that hash",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li4":
    "the Worker that receives anonymous answers keeps no logs, traces or analytics, and a test checks it",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li5":
    "comments are redacted when stored, and nothing is shown below the minimum group size, including by subtraction between groups",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li6": "every request is checked against the session, with access rules defined in one place",
90→  "legal.dpa.s05.li7":
    "traffic is encrypted in transit and storage is encrypted at rest. Only named operators can start a restore, and backups are kept for {restoreDays} days",
  "legal.dpa.s05.li8": "privacy tests that prove these properties must pass before a change is released",
  "legal.dpa.s06.title": "Sub-processors",
  "legal.dpa.s06.p1":
    "The Organization gives SurveyBeat general authorization to use the processors on the Sub-processors page. SurveyBeat imposes on each of them the same data protection duties as this agreement and stays responsible to the Organization for them.",
  "legal.dpa.s06.p2":
    "SurveyBeat tells the Organization's admins by email before it adds or replaces a sub-processor, early enough for the Organization to object. If the Organization objects on reasonable grounds and the parties cannot agree, the Organization may end the agreement.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.title": "Help, breaches and audits",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p1":
100→    "SurveyBeat helps the Organization answer requests from data subjects, and meet its duties under Articles 32 to 36, as far as the nature of the processing allows. If a request reaches SurveyBeat directly, it passes it to the Organization.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p2":
    "SurveyBeat tells the Organization's admins without undue delay after it becomes aware of a personal data breach, and gives what it knows about the nature of the breach, the data and people concerned, the likely consequences and the steps taken.",
  "legal.dpa.s07.p3":
    "SurveyBeat gives the Organization the information needed to show compliance with this agreement, and allows audits by the Organization or an auditor it names, with reasonable notice, normally once a year and again after a breach. The audit may not disclose other Organizations' data.",
  "legal.dpa.s08.title": "Return and deletion",
  "legal.dpa.s08.p1":
    "When the services end, SurveyBeat returns the Organization's personal data on request in a common machine-readable format and then deletes it, unless the law requires it to keep a copy. Copies in backups are overwritten as the {restoreDays}-day restore window passes. Anonymous Submissions are not personal data.   "legal.dpa.s09.title": "Transfers",
  "legal.dpa.s09.p1":
110→    "A transfer of personal data outside the EU and EEA takes place only under an adequacy decision, the EU Standard Contractual Clauses or another safeguard Chapter V of the GDPR allows. Comment text for AI processing goes only to endpoints in the EU.",

content.text:
1→# Anonymous Submissions store no person and no time, and are unlinkable at rest, not against a restore

**Threat model.** The Lead, Organization admins, and anyone using the product (UI, API, exports) must never be able to link a member to their Submission, and neither can an operator reading stored data, dumps, or R2 backups. We do **not** claim to defend against an operator who restores the Durable Object to a past moment (point-in-time recovery replays every write, including the one transaction that writes a Participation record and its Submission), reads Cloudflare's internal edge logs, or changes the code to start logging. Against that we use controls instead: only named people can trigger a restore, the privacy page states the 30-day restore window, and code changes on the submission path need review. The answer page's "Your name is never stored with your answers" is true of everything stored.

**Design.**
- Everything lives in the Organization's Durable Object. There is no per-Round object. The first Answer writes the Participation record and a Submission holding that one Answer in **one transaction**, which is how a double submission is rejected (a unique Participation record per Round and Person).
- An anonymous Submission stores only its Round, its Answers, and an Edit key hash. It stores **no person, no Invitation, and no time at all**, not even the day SPEC allows. A Participation record stores Round, Person, and the fact of answering, also with no time.
- Submission and Answer tables are `WITHOUT ROWID` with random 128-bit keys. Reads aggregate or sort by the random key. Dumps and backups are written in key order.
- **The anonymous Submission table has no person column, ever.** Attributed Submissions get their own table, so no bug can put a name on an anonymous answer.
10→- The Invitation token travels in the **URL fragment**, so the answer page GET (and every link scanner) never sends it. The page POSTs it to a **separate Submission Worker** with logs, traces, tail, Logpush, and Analytics Engine writes all off. That Worker logs error codes only. Tokens are stored only as hashes.
- The **browser generates the Edit key** and sends only its SHA-256 hash with the first Answer. Later Answers and changes carry only the Edit key. **No request may carry both an Invitation token and an Edit key**, and the server rejects one that does.

## Considered Options

- **Submissions in a separate Durable Object.** Rejected: without one transaction, a crash either loses the Answer or allows a second Submission, and the timing gap still exists.
- **Shuffled batch writes.** Rejected: buffered Answers are lost if the object is evicted, and it defends only against the restore threat we don't claim to cover.
- **A nullable person column shared with attributed mode.** Rejected: a single bug would put names on anonymous answers.

## Consequences

The glossary capitalizes "Leads" when listing lead, member, or viewer roles.

The glossary will list "members, viewers, Leads and admins" to match existing capitalization. The review flagged that "Every request is checked against the session" is too broad. Signed-in requests use sessions, but answer and submit requests use invitation tokens or edit keys. Unauthenticated routes like unsubscribe and delivery may also exist.

The glossary will be narrowed to say that signed-in requests use sessions, while answer and submit requests use invitation tokens or edit keys. A new s04.p3 addition will clarify that the system does not claim to defend against an operator who changes code to start logging.

Database backups are retained for restoreDays days to recover from a disaster. Restoring one replays every write, including the transaction that writes a Participation record and a Submission together. Only named SurveyBeat operators may start a restore; Organization admins and Leads cannot. Cloudflare edge logs cannot be read. A double space on line 52 will be fixed. The tparticipation.retention section also needs correction because it contains the same false "Deleting the Person" claim.

The retention table incorrectly claims that removing a Person deletes their Participation records. s04.p2 will be rewritten to clarify that submissions persist structurally because the table has no person column, not because of Recital 26. The in-app privacy page will not be expanded beyond Neon's edit key review.

The privacy.anonymity claim will remain unchanged. In dpia.md, the reminder opt-out description will be corrected to clarify that `GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe` only renders a confirmation page; the actual opt-out is performed via `POST /api/reminders/unsubscribe` using RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe-Post`.

# Working with long-running background tasks

Only submitting or queuing jobs is not sufficient to complete the task. The definition of done is the job has completed successfully and you have verified that it has produced all the expected outputs.
10→
This means you must see through the jobs completion by watching the job to ensure that its healthy, progressing, and working as intended.

## Tools available

There's two ways to watch jobs: monitor and loop. Decide which of the two you need, sometimes you need both.

### monitor — deterministic, actionable events

- Use a monitor when the event is a predicate a script can evaluate — an API response, an exit code, a port answering.
20→- Typical events: CI turning red, a PR comment or merge conflict, a PR becoming ready to merge, a dev server coming up or going down, a job reaching a terminal state.
- The monitor requires a script polls on a fixed cadence and stays silent until the predicate fires, so an idle job costs nothing. More on writing good monitoring scripts below.
- Examples of when to use:
  - Monitoring a PR — wake on CI breaking, merge conflicts, etc.
  - Checking if local tooling is up — wake on the service being unavailable, errors, etc.
  - All of these wakeup cases can be checked deterministically.

### loop — qualitative health that needs reading

- Use a loop when judging health requires reading the logs and system information to detect failing, faulty or stalled jobs. It uses a subagent which is more expensive but more thorough.
30→- Typical signals: the loss curve going unstable, a filtering pipeline producing garbage, throughput quietly degrading, faulty nodes throwing CUDA errors.
- A subagent reads the logs on a fixed cadence (say every 10 min) and reports what changed, so it costs a wakeup every cycle.
- Examples of when to use:
  - Checking on a training or data processing job — the subagent should scan for instability, degradation, faulty nodes, etc.
  - Monitoring system deployment health — the subagent should scan for 4xx/5xx, response times, resources, etc.
  - All of these wakeup cases are hard to describe deterministically and hard to fully enumerate, so it is better to use a subagent to validate.

## Good monitoring scripts

The monitor tool wakes you up every time you log to stdout. Wakeups are expensive, so only log if there is something actionable — but log it as early as possible, since staying silent delays the task. Plan accordingly: minimize the number of wakeups while still firing them as quickly as possible.
40→
### Planning

- Enumerate all terminal conditions.
  - For PRs, this includes the PR being merged or closed.
  - For long-running jobs, this includes the job completing or unrecoverable failures.
- Enumerate all other situations where a wakeup is needed.
  - For PRs, this would include when a comment arrives (there are four different types of PR comments), when CI fails, when a merge conflict arises, and when the PR becomes ready to merge (CI green, no conflicts, reviews complete, no blockers).
  - For an ML training job, this can be when the loss is unstable or the instance is preempted.
- Determine situations where the monitoring has to update what it is tracking. For example, for monitoring PRs, the latest commit hash may change as you push new commits.
50→
### Writing

- The monitoring script should poll every 30s. `watch_pr.py` defaults to
  `--poll-interval 30`. Lower intervals cause GitHub rate limits, especially
  with more than one watcher on the same token.
- Based on the planning, exit immediately on terminal conditions with FAILED, DONE, or CANCELLED, and log ACTION_REQUIRED for wakeups.
- Send all debug diagnostics — both your watcher's own trace and the monitored job's output — to a file, so a log line can never be mistaken for DONE, FAILED, or CANCELLED.
- The script should fail as early as possible. Emit a FAILED token immediately when any required condition reaches terminal failure. For example, if you are waiting on CI and any of them fail, emit FAILED immediately.
- Write the script to a durable location such as ~/.grok and name it something clear such as `ci_watcher.sh`.
60→- Key every log file the script writes on the pid or session id of the thing being watched. The paths are otherwise fixed, so a second job of the same kind silently clobbers the first one's log.

## Handling wake-ups

- Address errors or actionable events immediately. Look through the logs and debug the issue thoroughly before settling on a root cause, as long-running processes are generally expensive. Resubmit the job once it is fixed:
  - For PRs, this means repushing the changes and restarting CI (if needed).
  - For jobs, requeue or relaunch the job.
  - Always restart the monitor or loop so that it points at the new PR or job.
- If there are multiple jobs running, start debugging immediately when any jobs fail. Minimize total wall-time with completing tasks.

70→## Restarts

- Whenever you relaunch a job, always update the monitor.
- Monitors have a maximum 10-hour time limit, so be sure to restart them if you hit the time limit and if the task being monitored is still running.
- When you spawn a new monitor, make sure to kill any previous ones that the new one replaces. For example, if you fix a training run and respawn it, be sure to kill previous monitors, as irrelevant wakeups are expensive.

## Cleanup

- If a monitor is in a terminal state, kill the monitor, the loop, and the job. Dangling processes such as unkilled broken training runs are expensive. Then, address all issues if present.
- If an outdated monitor wakes you — that is, it is attached to an old or dead run — make sure to kill it.
80→- Do not leave detached workers, duplicate pollers, or orphaned watcher processes behind.

## Examples

### Example: maintaining a dev server

Suppose you just made some changes to the user's frontend code and would like to spin it up to test it. While you're testing it, you would like to know if the server goes down for any reason (if you made changes, for example). This is a great use case for the monitor tool. First start a React app in a background terminal, which reports its pid:

```
run_terminal_command(
90→  command="echo $$; npm start >~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/dev_server_$$.log 2>&1",
  timeout=0,
  description="Start the dev server on :3000",
  background=true
) # prints the pid 123456789
```

There are no terminal states, but there are two actionable events from the watcher: `http://localhost:3000` coming up and going down.

You want to be notified as soon as it is up so you can use it, and you want to be woken when it stops so you can address it — fix the code, restart the server, free the port. Both down paths quote the tail of the server's log, so the wakeup arrives with the error already in hand. Polling every 5s is a good cadence since you want to quickly fix it if it is down, and it is not expensive to poll.
100→
```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Log paths are keyed on the server pid so two dev servers cannot clobber each other.
PID=$1 URL=http://localhost:3000 DIR=~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks
LOG=$DIR/dev_server_$PID.log
up() { curl -fsS -o /dev/null --max-time 5 "$URL" 2>>"$DIR/watch_dev_server_$PID.log"; }
why() { tail -20 "$LOG" | tr -d '\r' | tr '\n' ' '; }

until up; do
110→  kill -0 "$PID" 2>/dev/null || { echo "FAILED: pid $PID exited before $URL came up: $(why)"; exit 1; }
  sleep 5
done
echo "ACTION_REQUIRED: $URL is up"

while :; do
  sleep 5
  up || { echo "ACTION_REQUIRED: $URL is down: $(why)"; until up; do sleep 5; done; }
done
```
120→
To spawn the monitor, point it at the pid `npm start` reported:

```
monitor(
  command='bash ~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/watch_dev_server.sh 123456789',
  description="Watch the dev server on :3000"
)
```

130→On the first wakeup the app is ready to use and you can start testing it. After that, you may be woken up if the server goes down. When you do:
- Read `~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/dev_server_<pid>.log` for the full compile error or port conflict and fix it.
- If the dev server survived, hot reload picks the fix up and the watcher recovers on its own, so leave the monitor running.
- If the process is dead, restart it with a fresh `run_terminal_command`, then kill this monitor and spawn a new one against the new pid.

### Example: PR monitoring

PR monitoring should stop when the PR is merged or closed, and it should wake up on:
- For comments, you should ask users how they would like to resolve them (which ones to address automatically, whether to respond / resolve, etc.), then store the decision for new future sessions. There are four different types of PR comments.
  - Inline review threads
140→  - Review bodies
  - Conversation comments
  - Commit comments
- Failing CI - most can be fixed in the code but sometimes they may be flaky. For flaky CI, just rerun them.
- Merge conflicts
- The PR becoming ready to merge — CI passes, no merge conflicts, reviews complete, no blockers, no unresolved inline threads. That wakeup is `kind: mergeable`. Tell the user they can merge now. It is not terminal; keep watching until merge or close.

You can find the example script bundled with this skill at watch_pr.py. It needs an authenticated `gh` CLI (`gh auth login`) and `python3`. Default poll is 30s; a lower poll rate may hit GitHub rate limits at higher concurrency. Transport errors (timeouts, resets, DNS) retry with backoff and jitter and do not print a line.

```
150→monitor(
  command='python3 ~/.grok/long-running-background-tasks/watch_pr.py "https://github.com/xai-org/grok-build/pull/123"',
  description="Watch PR 123"
)
```

### Example: training monitoring

For monitoring long training jobs, the terminal conditions are when the job either fails or completes. Further, many issues cannot be caught deterministically, so use a subagent to run a script for most of the high-level update, then scan the logs for errors such as faulty nodes or CUDA warnings.

160→The script below is bundled with this skill as watch_training.py. Run it with `--help` for every flag and for the run-directory and log-line layout it expects, since it parses nanoGPT stdout out of a Slurm run dir.

```md

1. python3 ~/.grok/skills/long-running-background-tasks/watch_training.py --run-name nanogpt_owt_124m_r1 --job-id 1234567 --target-val 3.00

How to report:
- Start with the job's state and if it changed, e.g. "still RUNNING" or "PENDING -> RUNNING".
- Copy the ISSUES line and the STATUS line from the monitor exactly as it is written, numbers and all. STATUS will include where the run is heading: how far along, iters left, the eta, and whether val loss is still coming down. We want val loss at or under 3.00.
170→- If the state didn't change, tell me that in one line and stop.
- If the job has finished or died, give me the state, the exit code, and the last ISSUES, and run these two for me:
  sacct -j 1234567 -D -X -P -o JobID,State,ExitCode,DerivedExitCode,Elapsed,NodeList,FailedNode
  tail -20 ~/train_logs/slurm-nanogpt_owt_124m_r1-1234567.out

```

Launch the scheduler on a 10 min interval, and spawn a monitor to be notified when the job crashes or succeeds.

180→```
scheduler_create(
  interval="10m",
  prompt: "...", # Copy from the prompt above.
)
monitor(
  # Wakes on pending/running/finished changes after the first observation.

  # transition would wake immediately on a just-submitted job.
190→  command='J=1234567; p=; while :; do s=$(sacct -nXP -j $J -o State|head -1); s=${s%% *}; s=${s:-PENDING}; if [ "$s" != "$p" ]; then case $s in COMPLETED) echo "DONE: $J"; exit;; PENDING|RUNNING|CONFIGURING|COMPLETING|REQUEUED|SUSPENDED|RESIZING) [ -n "$p" ] && echo "ACTION_REQUIRED: $J $p -> $s";; *) echo "FAILED: $J $s"; exit 1;; esac; fi; p=$s; sleep 30; done',
  description="Watch training run"

```

Launch both, so that we know when the job completes. When the monitor reports that the job has completed, cancel both the monitor and the scheduler, then determine next steps. Then:
- If it succeeded, simply present the results to the user.
- If it failed, debug the issue thoroughly, then fix and relaunch the job with new monitors attached. Make sure to have a thorough understanding of the issue before resubmitting, since training jobs are expensive. But always relaunch jobs so you don't waste the user's time.

70→4. **Statistical unlinkability & disclosure controls (`Unlinkability.privacy.test.ts`, `Results.privacy.test.ts`, `Themes.privacy.test.ts`):**
   - `Unlinkability.privacy.test.ts` and `Submissions.privacy.test.ts` (A4) prove that dumping `participation` and `submission` in key order yields no better than random-guess linkage across `rank`, `keyOrder`, `rowid`, and `sharedColumns` attacks.
   - `Minimum group size` (`>= 3`, default `4`, ADR 0004) blocks any `Result`, `Question` score, `Dimension` score, or subtraction-derived sub-group below `N`; no live `Result`s are shown while a `Round` is `Open`; `Lead` comments are unlinked from ratings and `Submission` order; `Comment theme`s require `>= 2` supporting comments and pass a 6-word anti-quote filter (ADR 0016, ADR 0019).
5. **Survival upon erasure (`Submissions.privacy.test.ts` A9):**
   - `directory.removePerson` sets `person.removed_at` and `membership.ended_at`. It deletes that `Person`'s `participation` rows, revokes `invitation`s, deletes `test_send`s, and deletes `person_index` in D1. The `person` row and membership history stay. There is no automated purge of that row, and no command that erases it or the membership history. That erasure is not available yet. `submission` and `answer` rows also stay. They are free of a `Person` column. A comment that still identifies its author remains personal data, so erasure of that comment is not done by `removePerson`.

### Residual Caveats Documented for Transparency

- **Free-text self-identification:** `redact` strips email local parts from the roster, emails, phones, handles, and URLs. It does not strip a display name that is absent from those local parts, a nickname, or a unique anecdote. The answer page says what is and is not removed (`apps/web/src/messages/answer.ts` `answer.comment.disclosure`). The in-app Privacy page has a separate `privacy.comments.body` in `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts`.
- **30-day Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR) window (ADR 0005):** Replaying the Durable Object write-ahead log (WAL) during a PITR restore could correlate writes made in the same transaction. SurveyBeat mitigates this through strict operator-only access controls, a hard 30-day backup expiry (`Policy.backupRetentionDays = 30`), and explicit user-facing disclosure (`catalog.ts` `privacy.restore`, `privacy.restoreTrigger`).

| Area | Specification / Policy Expectation | Live Schema / Code Reality |
| --- | --- | --- |

| **`Person` display name** | `Redaction.ts` accepts `name`, `firstName`, `lastName`, and `email` in a `Roster`. | `0003_person.sql` (`person`) stores `email` and no separate display-name column; roster redaction in `Organization` relies on `email` local parts until a display-name column is added. |

1→# Vendor DPA & Sub-processor Register (GDPR Art. 28) + Customer LIA Template

**Scope:** Active infrastructure and AI sub-processors used by SurveyBeat in `production`, plus a reusable **Legitimate Interest Assessment (LIA)** template for customer `Organization`s deploying SurveyBeat to EU `Team`s.  
**Vocabulary:** Domain terms follow [`GLOSSARY.md`](../../GLOSSARY.md).  
**Related Docs:** [`ropa.md`](./ropa.md), [`dpia.md`](./dpia.md), [`docs/infra.md`](../infra.md), [`0015-comment-ai-claude-haiku-via-openrouter-zdr-eu.md`](../adr/0015-comment-ai-claude-haiku-via-openrouter-zdr-eu.md).

## 1. Authorized Sub-processor Register (GDPR Art. 28)
10→
SurveyBeat uses only the sub-processors listed below. Chat integrations (Slack, Microsoft Teams) and fallback email providers (Postmark) mentioned in [`SPEC.md`](../../SPEC.md) are **not built or active** in the current codebase (`docs/infra.md`) and are excluded from this active register until implemented.

| Sub-processor | Service & Role in SurveyBeat | Personal Data / Content Processed | Processing Location | DPA & Transfer Safeguards (Chapter V) | Repo & Configuration Safeguards | Verification Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

PR 319 wording is being drafted for `legal.privacy.s03.tpeople.retention`, beginning with "While you are a Person in the Organization."

details.context_after:
| **Power imbalance (workplace context)** | Because `[Organization Name]` is the employer, `Team` members could fear retaliation if answers were attributable. SurveyBeat neutralizes this structurally: `Submission`s cannot be joined to `Person`s, `Minimum group size` blocks small-group exposure, `Lead`s see no live `Result`s while a `Round` is `Open`, and `Organization admin`s see no `Result`s. |
| **Reasonable expectations of `Team` members** | Periodic anonymous team feedback check-ins are standard in modern workplaces. An `Invitation` states the `Minimum group size` and that the name is not stored with the answers, and mentions `Redaction` and AI only when `ai_processing` is on. The answer page states the `Minimum group size`, what comment `Redaction` removes (`answer.comment.disclosure`), and the AI notice when AI is on. The 30-day backup window is on the in-app Privacy page only (`catalog.ts` `privacy.restore`). |
| **Autonomy & Right to Object (Art. 21)** | Participation in `Pulse`s is voluntary. `Team` members can opt out of reminders per `Pulse` (`GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe`, RFC 8058) or object to directory or reminder processing by contacting `[Internal HR / Privacy Contact]`. `directory.removePerson` sets `person.removed_at` and `membership.ended_at`, deletes `person_index`, `participation`, and `test_send`, and revokes `Invitation`s. The `person` row and membership history stay. There is no automated purge of the retained `person` row, and no command that erases that row or the membership history. That erasure is not available yet. |

content.newText: | **Autonomy & Right to Object (Art. 21)** | Participation in `Pulse`s is voluntary. `Team` members can opt out of reminders per `Pulse` (`POST /api/reminders/unsubscribe`, RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe-Post`; `GET` only shows the confirmation page) or object to directory or reminder processing by contacting `[Internal HR / Privacy Contact]`.

details.new_string: | **Autonomy & Right to Object (Art. 21)** | Participation in `Pulse`s is voluntary. `Team` members can opt out of reminders per `Pulse` (`POST /api/reminders/unsubscribe`, RFC 8058 `List-Unsubscribe-Post`; `GET` only shows the confirmation page) or object to directory or reminder processing by contacting `[Internal HR / Privacy Contact]`.
details.context_before:
| **Nature of data** | Directory & delivery metadata (work email, `Team` `Membership`, `Round` `Participation record` without timestamp). Stored `submission` and `answer` rows have no `Person` column (`ropa.md` §3). That is not a claim that every stored comment is non-personal data under Recital 26. A comment can still identify its author through a unique anecdote. Special-category data (Art. 9) is not solicited. |
| **Power imbalance (workplace context)** | Because `[Organization Name]` is the employer, `Team` members could fear retaliation if answers were attributable. SurveyBeat neutralizes this structurally: `Submission`s cannot be joined to `Person`s, `Minimum group size` blocks small-group exposure, `Lead`s see no live `Result`s while a `Round` is `Open`, and `Organization admin`s see no `Result`s. |
| **Reasonable expectations of `Team` members** | Periodic anonymous team feedback check-ins are standard in modern workplaces. An `Invitation` states the `Minimum group size` and that the name is not stored with the answers, and mentions `Redaction` and AI only when `ai_processing` is on. The answer page states the `Minimum group size`, what comment `Redaction` removes (`answer.comment.disclosure`), and the AI notice when AI is on. The 30-day backup window is on the in-app Privacy page only (`catalog.ts` `privacy.restore`). |
details.context_after:
| **Safeguards** | Zero-observability `SubmissionWorker`, encrypted storage, EU-pinned ZDR AI (if enabled), and documented internal policy prohibiting attempts to coerce or guess who wrote specific comments. |

tool_input.task:
Review SurveyBeat pull request 321 only. Repository chrisdoc/surveybeat-next, branch t3/gdpr-313-compliance-pack. The commit to review is 1de1aae3a0a4ebc82da420591a3a9c790faa6abc. Fetch origin and check out that commit. Confirm git rev-parse HEAD is exactly that SHA before you review. If it is not, stop and say so. An earlier review of e101a9ab is not a review of this commit.

Do not merge. Do not enable auto-merge. Do not post GitHub comments. Do not spawn subagents. Do not change product files. A throwaway checkout is fine if you remove it.

This is a docs-only compliance pack: docs/compliance/ropa.md, dpia.md, breach-response-runbook.md, vendor-dpa-register.md, plus a pointer in docs/infra.md. No product code, migrations, or new ADR. Glossary: Pulse, Person, Round, Submission, Answer, Invitation, Edit key, Organization, Team, Lead. Do not use User, Response, Respondent, or Responder.

Compare every claim you check with the live code. Prefer the code over the documents and over earlier reviews.

This commit is supposed to fix five defects. Reject the commit if any sentence is still false:

1. Reminder opt-out. GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe only renders the confirmation page (PageRoutes.ts renderUnsubscribePage). The write is POST /api/reminders/unsubscribe, including RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post. dpia.md and vendor-dpa-register.md must not call the opt-out a GET. Keep the separate fact that GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe?t= and GET /delivery?token= still put the live Invitation token in the query string (issue 311). Do not collapse those two facts.
2. vendor-dpa-register.md LIA nature-of-data row. Stored submission and answer rows have no Person column. That is not a claim that every stored comment is non-personal under Recital 26. A unique anecdote can still identify the author (ropa.md section 3). Do not accept a blanket anonymous-under-Recital-26 sentence.
3. ropa.md residual caveat on free-text self-identification. redact skips normalized local parts shorter than 2 characters (Redaction.ts). A one-character local part can remain as a word. A full email address is still replaced. A display name that is not in an email local part is not removed. person has no display-name column.
4. Person-row erasure. directory.removePerson sets person.removed_at and membership.ended_at, deletes person_index, participation, and test_send, and revokes invitations. The person row and membership history stay. There is no command, admin or self-service, that deletes that row. ropa.md P-1 and the section 4 discrepancy table must say that erasure is not available yet, not only that self-service export is missing or that an automated purge is missing.
5. EMAIL_DEAD_LETTERED. handleDeadLetter in EmailDelivery.ts logs sendId and state (the send state tag, or null), or no fields if the message is malformed. It does not log an error code. reason and code are logged by logOutcome on EMAIL_SEND_FAILED. The breach runbook and the ropa P-3 DLQ sentence must match that. The message body is not logged.

These earlier corrections must still hold: QuestionText is trimmed, length 1 to 200, and is not redacted before the AI call; R-05 residual stays Medium; R-01 stays Low for stored rows; answer links use #t=; email_send.content is StoredEmail JSON; browser keys are sb_edit_<roundId> and sb_answers_<roundId>; participation is (round_id, person_id) and is separate from submission; CancelRound deletes that Round's answers, submissions, and participation; redact runs in the Organization Durable Object; OpenRouter returns AiNotConfigured only when the key is missing or empty; the canary command names --stage production, https://dashboard.surveybeat.app, https://submit.surveybeat.app, and the two Cloudflare env vars; the OpenRouter CSAM retention exception is documented; BETTER_AUTH_SECRET is not a dashboard secret; no R2 bucket is declared.

External vendor terms stay unverified. Do not treat a missing executed Cloudflare, Google, AWS, or OpenRouter contract, street address, SCC, or DPF certificate as a docs defect when the page already says to verify it. Do not invent those facts.

Return REQUEST CHANGES or APPROVE. Name the SHA you reviewed. For each defect, cite the file, the sentence, and the contradicting source file and line. If nothing is false against the live code, approve.

rawInput.command:
python3 << 'PY'
import json, re, pathlib
for p in sorted(pathlib.Path("/tmp/pr321-comments").glob("*.json")):
    c = json.loads(p.read_text())
    body = c["body"]
    if "</details>" in body:
        verdict = body.split("</details>",1)[1]
    else:
        verdict = body
    verdict = re.sub(r"<!--.*?-->", "", verdict, flags=re.S)
    verdict = re.sub(r"<picture>.*?</picture>", "", verdict, flags=re.S)
    verdict = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", "", verdict)
    verdict = re.sub(r"\n{3,}", "\n\n", verdict).strip()
    print("="*70)
    print(c["id"], c["user"], c["path"], "reply_to", c["in_reply_to"], "line", c["line"])
    print(verdict[:2200])
    print()
PY

Verifying the plus-sign claim with a quick node/intl segmenter test.

The plus sign is not a word character in Unicode segmentation. The local part `abc+def` splits into three segments. The single-word matcher compares `abc` against the candidate `abc+def` and finds no match. The multi-word matcher requires multiple words, so the candidate is missed.

The candidate is split on whitespace, so `abc+def` remains a single word and is never matched. The full email address would be caught by the email regex. This leaves the local part exposed. The documentation's claim that roster emails are removed appears inaccurate.

Running a quick Node.js test with Intl.Segmenter to confirm the plus-sign behavior. Checking for existing tests covering plus signs. If the gap is confirmed, the documentation should clarify that local parts are split on dots, underscores, and hyphens only, not on plus signs.

The print output for "abc%def" appears corrupted, likely due to a format string issue.

The `%d` in the test string is being misinterpreted as a format specifier, producing `abcNaNef`. The shell or Node console is likely expanding the `%def` fragment.

The segmenter splits on both `+` and `%` as word breaks. The candidate extractor does not split on these characters, so local parts containing them remain whole. For example, `ab+c` is treated as a single candidate.

The segmenter splits `ab+c` into `ab` and `c`. Neither is a candidate, so the combined local part remains unmatched. Roster local parts are split only on `.`, `_`, and `-`.

The word matcher breaks on `+` and `%`, so local parts containing either character can remain in comments even when they are at least two characters long. The full email address is still replaced. This precise wording is preferable to the vaguer "attempts to match" phrasing, since prior reviews rejected overstated or imprecise claims. The vendor-dpa-register.md and ropa.md files need updates to avoid contradicting this behavior.

Reviewing five new comments on PR #321. The first two are on docs/compliance/breach-response-runbook.md and docs/compliance/dpia.md.

The remaining three comments are on docs/compliance/ropa.md, docs/compliance/vendor-dpa-register.md, and docs/compliance/breach-response-runbook.md. I will address all five items.

The PR 321 amend is still running. I will address the five new comments and then unwatch the pull request.

Track B is review-319-neon-3 REQUEST CHANGES. Two sentence edits are needed there. The amend task f96372a7 is still running. I will check its status next. Then I will push the changes. I will reply to CodeRabbit. Then I will launch review-321-neon-5.

I will check the amend task status and read the memory files. I am also deciding whether to read poteto-mode or use pstack-routing.

The amend is a terminal command, not a delegate, so I will check its output with get_command_or_subagent_output. I am also reading the long-running-background-tasks skill before proceeding.

I will read the leaving-pr-comments skill before posting any GitHub comments. I will also check memory files for issues 313 and 319. I will search for the t3 delegate_task schema to prepare for launching reviews. I can edit the 319 files while the 321 gate is still running, since I will not commit them until the gate exits.
The compliance-pack amend is still in the fence. I will check that commit, then answer the five review comments and apply the two disclosure fixes on the legal-pages branch.

description: Use whenever leaving comments on GitHub.
---

# Leaving PR Comments

Prefix every agent-authored comment left on the user's behalf with this GitHub
note callout:
10→
```md
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **<model> responding on behalf of <user>**

Actual comment starts here.
```

Use the verified public name of the model that wrote the comment, and the
user's name or GitHub login.
20→
If the harness does not expose a model name, use the harness name. Do not guess.

Before posting, check the entire comment, including quoted text and
attachments, for secrets and private details.

Keep the attribution inside the note and the actual reply outside it. The
context line must start with the robot emoji. Do not add a horizontal rule,
Setext underline, heading, signature footer, or a second attribution.

30→Apply this format to top-level PR comments, inline review comments, replies to
bots or reviewers, and written explanations used before resolving or
dismissing feedback. Do not add it to PR descriptions, commit messages, or text
the user explicitly asked to post verbatim without attribution.

Write the comment itself in a direct style:

- Lead with the conclusion.
- Cite the relevant code, behavior, check, or reproduction.
- Keep it concise and avoid filler, canned thanks, or status narration.
40→- Distinguish verified facts from judgment.

Preview the final Markdown before posting so quoting and blank lines render as
shown. After posting, verify that GitHub returned the comment or review URL.
Resolve a review thread only after its response was posted successfully.

matches.content: | **Data Controller** (Art. 34) | Controller-scope breach **likely to result in a high risk** to the rights and freedoms of natural persons (unless Art. 34(3) exemptions apply, e.g., strong encryption with uncompromised keys). | **Without undue delay** after triage confirms high risk. | Affected individuals (`Person`s / sign-in account holders), in clear and plain language. |

| **Critical (P1)** | Confirmed unauthorized access or exfiltration enabling **re-identification of anonymous `Submission`s** (e.g., `SubmissionWorker` logs enabled in `production` + captured traffic, unauthorized DO PITR restore + correlation, cross-`Organization` DO access); or mass exfiltration of D1 `auth_user`/`person_index` + active `auth_session` tokens. | Processor notice to affected `Organization`s **<= 24h**; Controller Art. 33(1) filing **<= 72h**; Art. 34 individual notice assessment immediately. |

| **High (P2)** | Unauthorized read/exposure of identifiable `Organization` or auth data without breaking `Submission` anonymity (e.g., `person`, `email_send`, `round_member`, `invitation`, `captured_email`, `auth_user` emails, or unredacted comment leaked via `MainWorker` before redaction/in error path); or confirmed sub-processor ZDR failure retaining `RedactedText` comments outside EU. | Processor notice **<= 24h**; Controller Art. 33(1) filing **<= 72h** if Controller data affected; Art. 34 risk evaluation. |
K -- No --> R["Customer data only. Processor notice already sent (Art. 33(2)). Do not file Art. 33(1). The customer Controller decides Art. 34. Log §6.4."]
N --> O{"Likely to result in HIGH risk to individuals (Art. 34)?"}
O -- Yes --> P["Notify affected individuals without undue delay (Art. 34)"]

| **T+0h – T+2h** | On-call Operator | **Contain immediately:** preserve logs/evidence first, then isolate the vector (see §5 Containment Playbook). Open incident channel and assign Incident Commander (IC). |

| **T+2h – T+6h** | IC & Engineering | **Triage & Scope:** determine exact tables/DOs/stages affected, count affected `Organization`s and `Person`s, check whether `SubmissionWorker` observability or AI endpoints were affected, assign Severity (`P1–P4`). If high risk to individuals is already apparent, start the Art. 34 assessment in this window, continue it as evidence arrives, and finish it without undue delay. Do not wait until T+24. |

## 3. Anonymity and residual identifiability of `submission` and `answer` rows (GDPR Recital 26)

Under GDPR Article 4(1) and Recital 26, data is outside the scope of personal data protection if it is rendered anonymous in such a manner that the data subject is not or is no longer identifiable, taking account of **"all the means reasonably likely to be used, such as singling out, either by the controller or by another person to identify the natural person directly or indirectly."**

The `submission` and `answer` tables (`packages/cloudflare/migrations/0008_submissions.sql`) are built so a stored row has no column that identifies a `Person`. That structural split is test-verified (`Submissions.privacy.test.ts`, `Unlinkability.privacy.test.ts`). It is not a claim that every stored comment is non-personal data. A comment can still identify its author through a unique anecdote that rule-based `Redaction` does not remove. Where that happens, treat the comment as personal data for retention and for rights requests. The controls below are what the schema and the ingestion path actually do:

- Before any `Answer` comment is written to SQLite, `recordFirstAnswer` and `saveAnswer` (`SqlRounds.ts`) call `redact` (`Redaction.ts`) inside the `Organization` Durable Object. `SubmissionWorker` forwards the raw answers over Durable Object RPC and does not redact them. The roster is the directory's `PersonRecord` list: email, and no display name. `redact` strips email local parts (split on `.`, `_`, and `-`), email addresses, phone numbers, `@handles`, and URLs, replacing them with `[name]`, `[email]`, `[phone]`, `[handle]`, and `[link]`. A candidate shorter than 2 characters is skipped, so a one-character local part can remain when it appears as a word. `+` and `%` are word breaks for the matcher and are not splits, so a local part that contains either can remain even when it is at least 2 characters. A full email address is still replaced. A display name that is not part of an email local part is not removed.

- **Free-text self-identification:** `redact` strips email local parts of at least 2 characters from the roster, plus emails, phones, handles, and URLs, when the word matcher can see them. It does not strip a one-character local part when it appears as a word, a local part that contains `+` or `%` (those are word breaks, and the candidate list does not split on them), a display name that is absent from those local parts, a nickname, or a unique anecdote. The answer page says what is and is not removed (`apps/web/src/messages/answer.ts` `answer.comment.disclosure`). The in-app Privacy page has a separate `privacy.comments.body` in `apps/web/src/messages/catalog.ts`.

| **`Person` display name** | `Redaction.ts` accepts `name`, `firstName`, `lastName`, and `email` in a `Roster`. | `0003_person.sql` (`person`) stores `email` and no separate display-name column; roster redaction in `Organization` relies on `email` local parts until a display-name column is added. |

| **Self-service Art. 15/17 endpoints** | `SPEC.md` §5.3 notes a `Person` can export and delete their personal data. | Live `SurveyBeatApi` (`PrivacyRegistry.ts`) currently exposes `directory.removePerson` (admin-initiated removal: sets `person.removed_at` and `membership.ended_at`) and `rounds.getMyHistory` (browser-local history + Team scores). No command, admin or self-service, deletes the `person` row or the membership history. That erasure is not available yet. Self-service data export is not implemented either. |

Checking legal.test.ts for assertions related to the reported sentences.

Only one match was found in legal.test.ts. Searching for "admin" and "hash" there, and checking messages.test.ts for glossary bans and length. The 319 edits are still pending from the interrupted session.

The 5 PR 321 comments are the primary task this turn. I will confirm each comment's disposition, reply to any that still need it, and launch neon-5. The 319 edits are also pending and can be handled now since no commit has been made.

Searching for snapshot tests that cover the full privacy page text. Reviewing legal.test.ts to see whether it checks full paragraphs or specific phrases. Checking line length and catalog style for readability. Drafting a proposed revision for s07.p1 that clarifies role-based access to leads and results.

The draft for s07.p1 now closely follows the review's wording. It states that an Organization admin does not grant access to any Team's Results, and that an admin sees a Team's Results only if they have a Membership in that Team. This wording is intended to match the existing Terms and allow neon-4 verification.

The Membership wording covers all three roles without needing an explicit list. ADR 0014 already allows admins to join teams, so the review's required phrasing is sufficient. s12.p1 matches the review exactly.

The s12.p1 revision will explicitly qualify that only invitation tokens and edit keys are stored as hashes. This avoids falsely claiming that session tokens, magic links, or codes are hashed. No additional sentence about raw session tokens is needed unless the review specifically requests it.

The source files were found in apps/web/src. Now searching the full 319 worktree for test expectations. The new wording uses glossary terms that should satisfy messages.test.ts. Checking legal.test.ts for privacy page assertions.

1→# SurveyBeat orchestration

Model roles for implementing and reviewing surveybeat-next issues.

## Routing

- Workers are Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini 4 Hydrogen; the reviewer is Opus 5.5.
- Workers implement in isolated worktrees and open PRs; Opus reviews before merge.
- Do not auto-merge.
10→- Open GDPR and Release 3 issues go through that orchestration.
- When Opus is unavailable, send delegated work, including PR review, to Neon instead of waiting for the Opus rate limit to lift.
- Gemini 4 Neon is available as antigravity model gemini-4-neon (option thought_level) and as opencode model opencode/gemini-4-neon (option variant).

Under GDPR Article 4(1) and Recital 26, data is outside the scope of personal data protection if it is rendered anonymous in such a manner that the data subject is not or is no longer identifiable, taking account of **"all the means reasonably likely to be used, such as singling out, either by the controller or by another person to identify the natural person directly or indirectly."**
--- timeline ---

If high risk to individuals is already apparent, start the Art. 34 assessment in this window, continue it as evidence arrives, and finish it without undue delay. Do not wait until T+24. |
| **T+6h – T+24h** | IC & Privacy/Legal | **Processor Notification (Art. 33(2)):** send initial written notice to all affected customer `Organization`s (`<= 24h` SLA) using Template §6.1, even if root-cause forensics are still underway. A customer-only breach (no SurveyBeat Controller data) ends SurveyBeat's external notices here; the customer Controller owns Art. 33(1) and Art. 34. |

A local part shorter than 2 characters is skipped. `+` and `%` are word breaks for the matcher and are not splits, so `abc+def` from `abc+def@example.com` can remain. This is a docs-only GDPR pack: docs/compliance/ropa.md, dpia.md, breach-response-runbook.md, vendor-dpa-register.md, plus a pointer in docs/infra.md. No product code changes belong in this PR.

Review the diff from 1de1aae3 to 6d12ff5e against the code, and spot-check that the earlier corrections were not reverted.

Claims that must match the code:
1. Redaction.ts: extractCandidateNames splits email local parts only on `.`, `_`, and `-`, and skips a normalized candidate shorter than 2 characters. Intl.Segmenter word breaks at `+` and `%`, so those characters are not candidate splits. A local part such as abc+def from abc+def@example.com can remain in a comment. EMAIL_PATTERN still replaces a full email address. person has no display-name column. The docs may say this in ropa.md section 3, dpia R-04 and R-05, and vendor-dpa-register.md (OpenRouter row and the LIA store-time bullet). They must not claim every local part is removed.
2. ropa.md section 3 heading is "Anonymity and residual identifiability of submission and answer rows (GDPR Recital 26)". It must not say every stored row is non-personal data. The section body must still say a unique anecdote can identify the author and is then personal data for retention and rights.
3. breach-response-runbook.md: T+2h to T+6h starts the Art. 34 assessment when high risk is already apparent, continues it as evidence arrives, and finishes it without undue delay, and says not to wait until T+24. T+24h to T+48h finishes an assessment that started at triage and is still open, and also finishes one that triage did not already show as high risk. Do not collapse those two rows into a single moment.
4. Still true, and must not have been reverted: the opt-out write is POST /api/reminders/unsubscribe (RFC 8058 List-Unsubscribe-Post); GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe only renders the confirmation page. GET /delivery?token= and GET /api/reminders/unsubscribe?t= still send the live token (issue 311) and R-07 residual stays Medium until that is fixed. Answer links use #t=. Stored submission and answer rows have no Person column, which is not a Recital 26 conclusion that every comment is non-personal. Person-row erasure is not available (removePerson does not DELETE FROM person). EMAIL_DEAD_LETTERED logs sendId and the send state tag, not an error code.

Glossary: Pulse, Person, Round, Submission, Answer, Invitation, Edit key, Organization, Team, Lead. Do not require the docs to say User, Response, or Respondent.

Return APPROVE only if every claim above is accurate on 6d12ff5e. Otherwise REQUEST CHANGES and quote the inaccurate sentence with the file and the code that contradicts it. Name the SHA you reviewed in the first line.

tool_input.task:
Review pull request 319 in chrisdoc/surveybeat-next. Read only. Do not edit files, commit, push, merge, comment on GitHub, or spawn subagents. Do not run the unit test suite or Organization.test.ts.

The branch is gdpr-305-legal-pages. The commit to review is exactly ae6a2681528152cc078b278e9e4a8ce0923f3376. Fetch origin and check out that commit. Run git rev-parse HEAD and refuse to review if it is any other SHA. review-319-neon-3 requested changes on ad6ca62a0134a39761a86863aab781c6692a908a. That review is not an approval of ae6a2681. The Opus review of e113ad04 is stale.

This PR is the public legal pages for issue 305. The new commit changes only apps/web/src/messages/legalPrivacy.ts and apps/web/src/site/legal.test.ts.

Verify these two sentences against the code, and spot-check that the earlier corrections on ad6ca62a were not reverted.

1. legal.privacy.s12.p1 must say Invitation tokens and Edit keys are stored only as hashes. It must not say that tokens in general, session tokens, magic-link tokens, or sign-in codes are stored only as hashes. Better Auth stores the raw session token in auth_session.token, the raw magic-link token, and the raw 6-digit sign-in code in auth_verification (packages/cloudflare/d1-migrations/0008_better_auth.sql; packages/auth/src/options.ts does not hash them). Only Invitation tokens and Edit keys are stored as hashes (migrations/0007_invitations.sql, d1-migrations/0005_invitations.sql, migrations/0008_submissions.sql). legal.dpa.s05.li3 already limits the hash claim to Invitation tokens and Edit keys. Do not require the public page to describe the raw Better Auth secrets; it must simply stop claiming every token is hashed.

2. legal.privacy.s07.p1 must say that being an Organization admin does not grant access to any Team's Results, and that an admin sees a Team's Results only with a Membership in that Team. Permissions.ts team.viewResults is granted to lead, member, and viewer, not to organizationAdmin. can() grants an organizationAdmin only when the action's grantee list includes admin. An admin who also has a Team Membership of lead, member, or viewer sees that Team's Results. ADR 0014 lets an admin join a Team. Do not ask for a product permission change. legal.terms.s03.p1 already says being an admin does not give access to any Team's Results.

Earlier sentences that must still be present: Question text is sent as written; the Edit key's first Answer sends only its hash and later Answers send the Edit key; erasing the Person record is not available yet; viewers are named in the DPA; the session check is limited to signed-in app requests; an operator who changes the code to start logging is outside the ADR 0005 claim; a comment that still identifies its author is personal data under Recital 26. The legal.test.ts expectations for the two new sentences must match the copy.

Glossary: Pulse, Person, Round, Submission, Organization, Team, Lead, Membership, Results, Invitation, Edit key. Do not require User, Response, or Respondent.

Return APPROVE only if both new sentences and the earlier corrections are accurate on ae6a2681. Otherwise REQUEST CHANGES and quote the inaccurate sentence with the file and the code that contradicts it. Name the SHA you reviewed in the first line.
